#1395. Player Ratings: Olympiacos 2-4 AC Milan – Hutchinson unplayable; Pulisic class

AC Milan completed a crucial comeback as they scored four goals against Olympiacos in the second half. One man in particular was behind the Rossoneri’s resurgence and below are the player ratings.

49 minutes into the game, it looked like Ruben Amorim and his men were heading for another disappointing defeat in the Europa League. Then, Omari Hutchinson decided enough was enough and inspired his teammates to a massive comeback.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

If you haven’t already, make sure to check out how we decide the player ratings. From the scale to what affects the rating, we have compiled everything there.

🥇 Hutchinson (9.5 – MOTM): Absolutely unstoppable in that second half. I mean, WOW! It’s not like a tap-in brought him to life either. He took matters into his own hands and scored an amazing solo goal, starting in Milan’s own half. Then the two assists on top of that, and the hockey assist for the fourth. Again, wow!

👎 De Winter (4.5): He has to take full responsibility for the second goal. It was truly a horrible pass and he then kept the goalscorer onside due to poor positioning. I actually don’t think he was good with his passing in the first half either, so the rating feels deserved.

👔 Amorim (7): I think he deserves a bit of credit as Milan’s first half was far from bad. They looked a lot more switched on compared to previous Europa League outings, and the goals could have been avoided through more player effort. Then, he made all the right substitutions.

Maignan (6): He made a great save in the first half to deny Martins. Some have suggested that he could have come out to parry the corner away on the first goal, but I don’t entirely agree. Anyway, he couldn’t do much about the second goal and was okay with his feet.

Gila (7): He was his usual aggressive self and that helped Milan on several occasions. Perhaps more so than his ability to win the ball back, however, it was his clearances that meant the most as he stopped some very good crosses. He also had a great overlapping run before the Rossoneri’s second goal.

De Winter (4.5): He has to take full responsibility for the second goal. It was truly a horrible pass and he then kept the goalscorer onside due to poor positioning. I actually don’t think he was good with his passing in the first half either, so the rating feels deserved.

Diawara (5): Touch and judgment. Those are the two things that let him down tonight. He put himself in too many tough positions due to the touch, and his judgment didn’t help when it came to anticipating the passes over the top. Just a really poor display, sadly.

Estupinan (5.5): He wasn’t terrible, but not good either. A rather quiet performance from him when you think about it, so it wasn’t enough for a pass here.

Jashari (6): It was a good opportunity for him and he sort of took it, I guess? It was very much a decent display overall. He had that great pass for Cisse that nearly led to a goal and also helped well in the build-up. However, he had a few misplaced passes and perhaps could have done more to stop Pirola in his tracks before the first goal.

Rabiot (6): In fairness to him, he did have a couple of important clearances defensively but in attack, he definitely didn’t add as much as we have seen in recent weeks. The goal contributions streak had to come to an end at some point. Still, overall, it was an okay performance.

Moreira (7): The goal obviously helps his rating a lot, especially since he remained composed, but he also had a couple of really nice switches to Hutchinson on the other side. He was a tad wasteful in some situations, in my opinion, but a decent display plus a goal deserves a good rating.

Hutchinson (9 – MOTM): Absolutely unstoppable in that second half. I mean, WOW! It’s not like a tap-in brought him to life either. He took matters into his own hands and scored an amazing solo goal, starting in Milan’s own half. Then the two assists on top of that, and the hockey assist for the fourth. Again, wow!

Cisse (7.5): Another goal for the youngster! I thought he did well at left-wing, nearly scoring that goal despite the goalkeeper’s challenge, but he continued to do well at centre-forward. The movement and header on the goal proved once again that he’s got it.

Ramos (5.5): Similarly to Estupinan, as both were taken off at half-time, it was more a quiet performance than it was a really bad one. That said, the No.9 had a couple of moments on the counter that could have been handled better.

Musah (6.5): It’s hard to put my finger on exactly what he changed, but he brought something to the game which helped Milan play better. Could absolutely be his movement as he covered a lot of ground and wasn’t afraid to drive forward either.

Pulisic (8.5): World class is probably the best way to describe him. You could immediately see the difference he was going to make, although perhaps no one predicted that goal. It was a tremendous strike to complete the turnaround for Milan. Tremendous! And then he got the assist for Moreira. We can forgive the miss just before that.

Tomori (6.5): Almost a 7 for him, but it’s possible that I might be influenced by just how poor De Winter and Diawara were. Anyway, the Englishman returned with a strong performance and showed that he’s one to rely on.

Terracciano (6): He’s the master of always opting for the easy way out, but in this case, that was probably exactly what Milan needed.

Amorim (7): I think he deserves a bit of credit as Milan’s first half was far from bad. They looked a lot more switched on compared to previous Europa League outings, and the goals could have been avoided through more player effort. Then, he made all the right substitutions.

Remember that you can share your ratings in a fancy infographic (updated for this game!) by clicking ‘Share’ after submitting them.

🚨Olympiacos head coach Imanol Alguacil on AC Milan’s 15-minute comeback against Olympiacos:

We lost today because we failed to do our assignment on Omari Hutchinson.

We initially had a plan to contain him and keep him quiet. We wanted to stop him receiving the ball facing our defenders, because once he turns and starts running at you, the problem becomes much bigger.

And for most of the first half, we did it.

Even in the second half, for some time, we managed it.

Hutchinson started taking responsibility.

And suddenly our defensive structure was changing because everybody was worried about him.

We actually removed two players from marking him because we wanted to protect the space around him.

He got the better of Onyemachi, scored the first goal and suddenly Milan believed again.

I was angry with my players because we allowed him to get into those situations.

When you are 2–0 up at home against AC Milan, you cannot allow one player to turn the entire match around.

There is very little you can do when you have a winger running at you with that much confidence.

He is small, he is close to the ground, his balance is excellent and he changes direction very quickly.

That makes him extremely difficult to defend.

If you go to ground, you risk catching his leg instead of the ball and getting a yellow card.

If you don’t go to ground, he pushes the ball past you and runs.

So the defender has to make a decision in one second.

Our defenders decided to give him the space.

And once he realised they were backing away from him, he became even more confident.

That is when you know you have a problem.

Because a winger like that doesn’t need five chances.

Give him one successful dribble and suddenly he believes he can beat everybody.

We went from controlling the game to defending like we were frightened of one player.

We should have made somebody stay close to him instead of allowing him to receive the ball and face our defence.

But football punishes you when you hesitate.

We went from a perfect win to a perfect defeat in fifteen minutes.

Because I don’t think we were the worse team.

I don’t think our football suddenly disappeared.

We simply failed to deal with one player when the game became chaotic.

I told him, ‘You have a very good player there.’

Because if Hutchinson learns how to control games like that consistently, not just moments, then Milan have something very special.

And unfortunately for us, we allowed him to do it.”

#1394. Locatelli tells young Juventus fans he has learned to accept long knee layoff

Juventus captain Manuel Locatelli has called his knee injury one of the hardest spells of his career. Answering questions from young members of the club, he said his recovery is on track and that he has learned to live with a long wait.

Manuel Locatelli has not played since early September, and the Juventus captain admits the time away has been tough. Speaking in a new episode of the club’s Junior Reporter series, in which children from the Juventus membership programme interview a first team player, the midfielder was open about how he is coping.

As ANSA reported on Tuesday evening, Locatelli put the injury alongside Italy’s failure to reach the World Cup as the lowest points of his time as a professional.

Locatelli explained that he hurt his knee and now has to stay off the pitch for a long time. He said he feels good and that the work is going well, much of it in the gym rather than on the grass.

“I miss playing football so much, so much, but I have learned to accept this situation,” he told the young reporters, according to the quotes carried by Calciomercato.com. He added that he knows he has to give it time, and that he must do his best to come back in good shape.

On the national team, he did not hide the pain of missing out on the tournament. “When you lose, and lose like that, it is a moment of suffering,” he said.

The problem dates back to 6 September, when Locatelli sprained his right knee in the 1-1 home draw against Milan. Two days later Juventus confirmed in an official medical update that he had undergone surgery in Lyon to suture the external meniscus. Dr Bertrand Sonnery-Cottet carried out the operation with club doctor Marco Freschi in attendance, and rehabilitation started the following day.

The club gave no return date at the time. ANSA now says the captain expects to be available again in the first months of 2027, while Football Italia reports that he is not expected back in full training before March.

Locatelli also spoke about leadership. He said becoming captain was an ambition he had from the moment he arrived from Sassuolo in 2021, and he credited Giorgio Chiellini, Leonardo Bonucci and Danilo for showing him what it means to be present for the group every day. His childhood idols, he said, were Pavel Nedved, Gianluigi Buffon, Alessandro Del Piero and Francesco Totti.

The club tied him down in April, when he signed a new contract until June 2030.

His absence has forced Luciano Spalletti to reshape his midfield for most of the autumn, a problem we looked at when Thuram and Locatelli were both missing earlier this month.

Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League on Thursday on the back of a 4-0 win over Venezia, and go to Como on Sunday with a clean bill on the disciplinary front, as covered in our piece on the matchday 12 rulings. Their captain, for now, remains a spectator, but by his own account a patient one.

#1393. Lethal Trent Alexander-Arnold sends Tuchel a statement in England victory

Thomas Tuchel has never been inclined to place much faith in the most famous right-back at his disposal, Trent Alexander-Arnold, once of Liverpool, now of Real Madrid, and – back in an England shirt – still capable of changing games in the blink of an eye.

England always looked likely to defeat a beleaguered Czech Republic team down to 10 men with just 25 minutes played, but it still required one man to conjure the moment of inspiration in this Nations League tie. This was the first cap in 15 months for the right-back now known simply as “Trent” in an England shirt – as well as his Real Madrid jersey – rather than the six syllables of his surname. With the game level at half-time, two minutes into the new half, he twice won the ball before landing a cross on the head of Anthony Gordon for the first goal.

TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3 goals in his last 3 games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/xmqPIULJ24

Will the Alexander-Arnold with England experiment survive? One feels that Tuchel will need a little more to convince him to abandon whatever reservations he has about the Liverpudlian. A week short of his 28th birthday, Alexander-Arnold was winning just his 35th cap. His Real Madrid team-mate Jude Bellingham, a second-half substitute, was earning his 58th cap less than two months after his 23rd birthday. Bellingham was on as captain in place of the man he replaced, Harry Kane, scorer of England’s second. Bellingham’s international career has taken a much less rocky path than that of his Real team-mate.

Having missed the World Cup finals this summer, and had little good fortune around previous tournaments, one wonders if Euro 2028 might be the watershed moment for Alexander-Arnold. Either way, against opponents who sit back, he is lethal when it is time for the big delivery. Alexander-Arnold may not have the breadth of England experience that some of his peers have accumulated, but he does have plenty of experience of big games.

“I make that run time and time again,” Gordon said of his anticipation of the Alexander-Arnold cross, “but only a set number of players have that ability, that technique and the bravery to risk a mistake to play that pass. And that’s why I have been dying to play with him [Alexander-Arnold]. He’s been on his own journey but has trained really well this week. He should have played more. Sorry – he would have loved to have played more.”

A Freudian slip from the Barcelona winger, another Liverpudlian in Spain, who himself has barely put a foot wrong for England of late. He has three goals in three games for England, including the World Cup semi-final against Argentina. This was an England team that Tuchel fine-tuned, first to give a rest to Bellingham and in other quarters, too. Lewis Hall started at left-back. Trevoh Chalobah won his third England cap at centre-back. Alex Scott, of Bournemouth, was given his debut off the bench in the second half and Rio Ngumoha won the second cap of his England career, just one month after his 18th birthday.

As for Kane, his 87th goal for England now puts him within two goals of Robert Lewandowski, among four greats in the seven ahead of Kane on the all-time international goalscorers’ list. By the end of this international break the England captain should have equalled Peter Shilton’s record 125 caps. It has been an astonishing career even if it ends tomorrow. Following the missed penalty against Spain, Kane was again the man in the right place at the right time when Morgan Rogers’s shot was blocked in the second half.

“Strange to get an early red card,” Tuchel said. “Not the best for the team and spectators. It’s an awkward one, but we kept going, got a win and that’s what counts.” Not quite a vintage Czech Republic team, either, and when their best player of the opening stages, the attacking midfielder Pavel Sulc, of Lyon in Ligue 1, was dismissed after 25 minutes, it certainly did not become any easier for the home team. Sulc, the Czech player of the year in 2025, had mistimed a tackle on Elliot Anderson, which on a VAR review, the Turkish referee Umut Meler decided was worthy of an upgrade from yellow to red. It was high on the right calf of the England midfielder.

Czech Republic DOWN TO 10 MEN! 🟥Pavel Šulc sees red for a dangerous challenge on Elliot Anderson#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/B2YOLuS0vL

England had looked once more a little open to the counter-attack in the early stages, with Sulc one notable runner. This was not an opponent of the quality of Spain and Tuchel’s players were able to recover the situation. When they lose the ball in the opposition’s half, England tend to look vulnerable.

Even before the red card Rogers had hit a post. Myles Lewis-Skelly, playing in midfield, was booked for a foul on Lukas Serv and was pursued thereafter by the Czech players hoping to get an upgrade on the yellow card. He was substituted at half-time, with Eberechi Eze on in his place.

“I spoke to Ant [Gordon] at half-time,” Alexander-Arnold said later to ITV, “and I said if I’m getting in those spaces make sure you get to the back post. You don’t expect to get it that fast, but it did and it worked.”

Two minutes after the break, Alexander-Arnold suddenly burst into life. He won the ball back in his own area and then drove forward in search of the return. When that did not come, he raced back to win the ball again and unleashed one of those right-footed outswingers to the back post, where Gordon guided in the header. “Really proud to score that,” Gordon said, “because I can’t tell you the number of hours I’ve spent practising headers.”

Kane scored the second just a minute before he was replaced and Bellingham took the captain’s armband and the role as a No 9. One day someone will have to step into those goalscorer’s boots on a permanent basis and try to replace Kane – although it may be a while yet.

Thomas Tuchel has backed Jude Bellingham as a future England captain after giving him the armband in the victory over the Czech Republic.

In the absence of Declan Rice, who was vice-captain at the World Cup, Bellingham assumed the role when he came on for Harry Kane, who is now in his 10th season as England captain and also scored in the 2-0 win in Prague.

Tuchel, who needs to check on Bellingham ahead of Saturday’s game against Croatia after a “niggle,” has praised the midfielder’s attitude during the extended international break one year after he was back from an injury but left out of the squad.

“If you are the captain at the end of these matches, you can be the permanent captain,” Tuchel said when asked whether Bellingham could eventually lead the team. “He was the captain against New Zealand before the World Cup. It is always a reward and always an honour.

“I think he loves to be with us at the moment. That’s what I feel, and we had this small talk today about his role. We felt in our hearts or our stomachs to say ‘let’s go again, let’s start again’ and also our heads told us maybe 30 minutes is enough for this match because he hasn’t played in this quick turnaround through this season. He has done it before, but not in the season, so we didn’t want to be the first ones to try that.

“But even in this little encounter, you can see that he’s confident and happy to help from the bench. So it’s a reward. It’s good. He had a little niggle at the end of the match, so hopefully it’s nothing serious, and he’s available for Croatia.”

Nico O’Reilly is a doubt for the Croatia match in Rijeka and there are also concerns over Ezri Konsa, who was on the bench but not fit enough to play.

Trent Alexander-Arnold provided an assist for Anthony Gordon in the Real Madrid full-back’s first cap in 15 months. Gordon, meanwhile, has now scored in the first two Nations League games of the campaign and is staking his case to be an indispensable player for Tuchel.

“He’s getting there. He’s defending his shirt, he’s defending his position, an excellent performance again after his performance against Spain,” Tuchel said.

“He was very decisive today and had an excellent goal. It was very, very difficult, but the technique and finishing was excellent. He scored against Spain, so he has decisive actions and he’s defending his shirt and his position. He does it on the highest level and he’s a very important player.”

England returned to winning ways with a 2-0 win over Czech Republic in Prague.

Pavel Sulc’s first-half red card after a VAR review of his clumsy challenge on Elliot Anderson took the sting out of the initially lively hosts and Anthony Gordon gave Thomas Tuchel’s men a deserved lead early in the second half.

The forward headed home a fantastic cross by Trent Alexander-Arnold, who was making his first start under the German coach, before skipper Harry Kane scored to settle any nerves.

So who played well for England and who failed to impress? Rate each player with our voting tool, and have your say in the comments.

I thought we were very professional second half. We stepped up and needed to be more dynamic, bring more urgency into our play, which we did. We kept that intensity going and and the effort was till there. Deserved victory.

Strange to get an early red card. Not the best for the spectators, not the best for the team. It’s an awkward one. But we got the win.

To guide it into the goal, there was an awful lot [for Anthony Gordon] to do. Good pass, good goal. Both full-backs were good. The position in the second half suited Trent more than the position in the first half. Lewis was excellent on the other side.

We have used all the outfield players after two matches so credit to all of them. Now it’s important to relax and enjoy the evening, do a good recovery and prepare for Saturday.

I think it was good. They go down to 10 men and it should be easier for us to win the game, But in fact it makes it more difficult. They get very compact and defend with a lot of players around the box and it’s hard to break them down.

We got that [goal] at the start of the second half which is what we needed. The longer it’s 0-0, it gets harder and harder and harder.

[Where do you place your assist?]  It’s up there for sure. I spoke to Ant at half-time and said if I get into those half-spaces I’m looking to put it in so make sure you get to the back post. I didn’t expect it to work so quickly.

He’s a willing runner, great to play with him. I saw the run and was able to execute the pass,

It’s always a pleasure and an honour to represent my country. It’s been a long time. I’ve always believed that I can play for England and I want to. The manager’s given me the opportunity and I tried to do what he wanted me to do to the best of my ability and I hope he’s happy with how I played.

🦁 #1301Alex Scott reflects on a special night, earning his first senior England cap 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @England pic.twitter.com/lC34bAPbbd

It was good, quite dominant. We created a lot of chances but without the quality. When they went a man down, we were too passive at times. We need to be dominant, as I said earlier, go for the throat and put teams away.

I said that to him [Trent, on the quality of the ‘assist’]. I make that run time and time again but only a set number of players have that ability, that technique and the bravery to risk a mistake to play that pass. And that’s why I have been dying to play with him. He’s been on his own journey but has trained really well this week. He should have played more. Sorry, he would have loved to have played more.

I’ve missed playing with Hally. He’s a good lad. We had great chemistry at Newcastle and it’s great to share this stage with him.

It’s my only header. I’d be the worst header of the ball you’ll ever see. Really happy, resally proud to score that because I can’t tell you the number of hours I’ve spent practising headers.

Perfectly competent and signs of promise in the left-back/left-wing axis. England looked too open against 11 men and better teams – hola España – may have capitalised on the sloppiness. But once Sulc was sent off, England gradually turned the screw and created a hatful of chances, running out easy winners.

Another tidy save from Kovar when Bellingham receives a pass from the left, strides towards the D, then drives a daisy-cutter towards the left of goal. The keeper swoops down early to turn it behind with a stiff wrist.

Two minutes of stoppage time are signalled as England try to pen the home side in their own half.

Tuchel has kept the back four on the pitch for the 90 minutes. He was not entirely happy with them in the first half – or his body language suggested that, anyway. But it is a welcomed clean sheet for England after the chaotic defeats to Spain and France.

Ngumoha is enjoying himself and showing off some excellent close control.

Scott and Eze smash shots over the bar from 22 yards within a minute of each other.

Rogers’ diagonal cross is chested down by Eze as he sets up an opportunity to shoot in the area but a defender hacks it away. Ngumoha pounces on the loose ball and plays a neat reverse pass with the outside of his boot to Rogers on the underlap. Rogers goes for power rather than lift to find Eze or Bellingham and the keeper makes another smart save.

Gibbs-White’s pace and direct running have the beating of Chaloupek and he tees up Eze to hammer a left-foot shot that seemed to be arrowing into the net until Kovar stuck up his right hand to paw it over.

Gordon stops, then from a standing start drives past bursts past Chaloupek to the byline and stands up a near-post cross that Rogers flashes wide.

Czech Republic break after England’s attack down the right hits the skids. Hlozek gallops down the middle and lets fly before Scott can catch him. Trafford sees it all the way, dives to his right to save and gathers the loopy effort from the rebound.

Slama hounds Ngumoha into conceding a corner as the Liverpool winger slips under pressure.

Jude Bellingham is wearing the England captain’s armband again. He was also wearing it during the pre-World Cup camp against New Zealand. Thomas Tuchel explained afterwards that the player with the most caps is skipper when Harry Kane is subbed off. Bellingham is also playing centrally, as a False Nine.

Bellingham → KaneNgumoha → SakaScott → Anderson.

England have switched to the Revie Plan with Bellingham as the deep-lying centre-forward.

Czech Republic 0 England 2 (Kane) Eze plays Rogers in down the left of the box. He gets there but falls under the tackle of Krejci, knocking the ball to Kane who thumps it through Hranac’s legs with his left foot from about seven yards.

KANE DOUBLES ENGLAND'S LEAD 🔥Harry Kane in the right place at the right time for the Three Lions 🦁#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/Od9x5kXOsH

As Sam Matterface points out. England having a left-footed left-back has added an extra dimension to their attacking play. Corner on the right for England who procrastinate so long over their positions the referee warns them but does not take it off them. Krejci and Kane have their arms around each other as the ball comes in and the Czech captain pulls Kane to the ground but the referee waves play on.

TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3️⃣ goals in his last 4️⃣ games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/iej0PCW8Ar

Man City used ‘sham’ sponsorships in £830m cheating scheme

Manchester City arranged “sham” sponsorships in a near-£1bn plot to flout Premier League rules, an independent commission has found.

It was confirmed on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges related to “serious breaches” of the league’s financial rules, with the commission also upholding all but one in relation to their failure to co-operate with an investigation spanning over three years.

The commission found that, of £949.94m City claimed in commercial income over a nine-year period, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the remaining £830.69m illicitly paid by their Abu Dhabi owners.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Uefa Nations League match between Czech Republic and England from Slavia Prague’s Eden Stadium. The home side, 49th in the Fifa rankings, scrambled their way to World Cup qualification with victories in the play-offs in penalty shoot-outs over Ireland and Denmark, promptly stank Group A out in Mexico/Canada/United States, drawing with South Africa but losing to South Korea and Mexico to finish last.

Miroslav Koubek, their 74-year-old manager, the oldest in the competition’s history, promptly stood down and has been replaced by their first foreign head coach, Santi, the former Atlético Madrid centre-half, who spent 15 years moving from managing Spain’s U17s, to the U19s and then the U21s. Little wonder, given his CV, that he is looking to refresh his squad with a transfusion of young players, a requirement made all the more urgent by the international retirement of stalwart centre-forward Patrick Schick and the absence of West Ham’s Tomas Soucek who damaged his ankle in that 3-0 defeat by Mexico on June 25 and has not kicked a ball since.

Santi started his stint in charge and this campaign in Group A3 with a 2-1 defeat by Croatia but there were some very positive signs – they set up as a 4-3-3 in classic Spanish/Cruyff style and pressed like dervishes. England, who conceded three goals when players made mistakes when subjected to aggressive pressing in their opening 3-2 defeat by world champions Spain, will have to find better solutions tonight, either by holding their nerve or counterpressing with fewer mistakes.

Given England are ranked 45 places higher, their results, if not all performances, at the World Cup were commendable and the way in which they rattled Spain and should really have given themselves a bulwark against the comeback by converting their penalty at 2-1 up,  an away win should be relatively straightforward. But they did lose on their last visit to Prague in a Euro 2020 qualifier having won 5-0 in the home leg.

#1392. The Musiala case causes a huge outcry in Germany!

The controversy surrounding Jamal Musiala is far from falling on Bayern Munich. For several days, the Bavarian management’s comments on the future of the attacking midfielder and his imposing salary have sparked a wave of indignation in Germany. After Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, it is now Maik Franz who has stepped up to the plate. Guest of the show Doppelpass on Sport1the former defender did not mince his words to denounce the attitude of the Munich board, which he considers particularly inappropriate towards a player facing health problems. At the heart of this controversy, the statements of Rummenigge, who publicly questioned Musiala’s salary conditions in view of his physical difficulties and his level of performance.

An outing which provoked numerous reactions, notably from Maik Franz: “what the Bayern leaders are doing, and I’m not talking about Kompany and Eberl, who are behaving in an exemplary manner, but about MM. Hoeness, Dreesen and Rummenigge, is pathetic and even, in my eyes, constitutes harassment. We can discuss a player’s performance. But it is not appropriate to talk publicly about an illness and the salary associated with it, at this level. We must not forget that Jamal tried everything to come back. He showed a lot of courage and transparency in discussing his diagnosis. For this to turn against him today is not acceptable. To be completely honest, we are no longer in “Mia san Mia”, but in “Mia san money”. Money takes precedence over people. And this must not happen.”.

The controversy even went beyond the borders of Bavarian management to affect the locker room. Michael Olise actually liked an Instagram post from Fabrizio Romano relaying the press release from FIFPRO, the international players’ union, which called on Bayern to respect Jamal Musiala. A particularly notable gesture from the French international, renowned for his discretion on social networks. This support takes on an additional dimension as Bayern wish to extend Olise’s contract, currently linked to the club until 2029. Maik Franz also underlined the risk that this affair could represent for decision-makers: “With Michael Olise, you may have the next best player in the world in your ranks. He too must extend and receive a big salary. But you keep in mind that if you got sick or injured and didn’t perform, you would be publicly thrown out to waste. Frankly, I don’t think they did themselves any favors.”.

FIFPRO also strongly criticized Bayern’s communication, saying contractual issues should be discussed privately with the player and his representatives. The union notably recalled that an injury or decline in form did not justify publicly calling into question salary conditions already agreed upon. While Musiala tries to regain his best level after a long period of absence, the Bavarian club finds itself under fire from critics. Between the declarations of its leaders, the exit of Maik Franz and the remarkable gesture of Olise, the file has become a real image issue for Bayern Munich…

Christian Pulisic has insisted that AC Milan are growing together as a team under Ruben Amorim, after the comeback win over Olympiacos.

In what had been a running theme in their opening four Europa League games, Milan started slowly and found themselves two goals down in Greece. The first was attributed as a Mike Maignan own-goal, while there was no doubt that Jota Silva got the second.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Diego Moreira added a fourth in the dying seconds to make sure of a much-needed win. Pulisic came off the bench and left his mark on the game with his goal and assist for the Moreira’s at the end, and he spoke to Sky after the final whistle. His words were relayed by MilanNews.

#1390. Como beat AEK with eight players missing, then faded late before hosting Juventus

Como beat AEK Athens 1-0 to reach 12 points in the Champions League, despite eight unavailable players and a late drop in intensity. Juventus visit the Sinigaglia on Sunday, but must first play Omonia on Thursday.

The narrow victory over AEK was Como’s third straight win in the Champions League. It leaves them close to the knockout stage. It also offers the latest look at Juventus’s next league opponents, on the same ground.

The win came with a stretched squad. Fàbregas told Sky Sport that the absentees were either injured or left out of the Champions League squad list. Making so few changes was, he said, a first in his coaching career. That is a thin bench ahead of a league weekend.

The scoreline flattered AEK in places. Lucas Da Cunha missed a first-half penalty, and Nico Paz hit the post. At the other end, goalkeeper Robert Sánchez made two important saves before the break. Milla’s goal made him the 11th different player to score for Como in this season’s competition. No other team in the Champions League has had that many different scorers. UEFA named him Player of the Match.

Como had been scoring freely before Matchday 5. On Matchday 4 they won 9-1 away to Lens, a result that put them fourth at the halfway point of the league phase. AEK proved a harder problem. They held Como up for long spells and were difficult to break down.

The final stretch was the concern. Fabio Capello put it to Fàbregas that Como had dropped off badly in the last 20 minutes. The coach replied that he did not yet have the experience to stay calm in such moments. The late fade is consistent with a group short on fresh legs.

Fàbregas also set out his priorities. He said the win brought Como close to at least a play-off place, but that qualification was not yet secured. In the same breath, he stressed that Serie A matters more to the club. That message points straight at Sunday’s meeting with Juventus.

Juventus have their own European commitment first. Kick-off in Turin, in the Europa League league phase, is at 20:00 UTC. Juve go into that game fifth with 10 points from four matches. Omonia are 18th with six. Sam Barrott of England will referee, with Darren England on VAR.

That schedule cuts into any advantage from Como’s fatigue. Both sides will carry European minutes into the weekend. Juve, however, will have had two fewer days to recover.

The league table adds weight to the fixture. Como sit fourth in Serie A, eight points ahead of Juventus. A home defeat would leave a depleted Como squad with a reduced cushion. A Juve win would close the gap at the end of a demanding week.

Como’s Champions League campaign continues away to Real Betis on 9 December, and the league phase ends with a trip to Barcelona on Wednesday 27 January 2027. After Sunday’s 13th-round meeting at the Sinigaglia, Juventus host Udinese at 18:00 on Sunday 6 December.

#1385. Amorim analyses Olympiacos comeback, Hutchinson’s potential and need to cut out mistakes

AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim believes that the comeback win over Olympiacos is something that could ‘change the future’.

After 50 minutes of the game on the outskirts of Athens, it looked like Milan were heading for a fourth defeat in five Europa League games. Lorenzo Pirola crashed a header in off the bar via Mike Maignan, then Jota Silva scored a second early in the second half.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Then, out of almost nowhere, Omari Hutchinson inspired a run of three goals in 15 minutes. Firstly he scored a goal of his own with a brilliant solo run, then he set up Alphadjo Cisse for his 10th goal of the season, then he crossed for a Christian Pulisic volley to make it 3-2.

Diego Moreira added a fourth late on to make sure of the points. Amorim spoke to Sky after the final whistle to give his thoughts on what was a rollercoaster night, but one that thankfully ended well. His words are via MilanNews.

Will this second half change the Europa League season?

“It definitely changes our future. We played well in the second half, but we made a lot of mistakes again and we need to improve. But we got a lot of players back, it was a positive night.”

“It’s better to finish games like this, winning obviously. We have a lot of work to do to be a very strong team, but the spirit is there. It’s the start of something.”

“I think this is the biggest problem: focusing on the small details like set pieces, goalkeeping, and the plays we need to make. It comes with time and experience.

“The technical aspect is fine, but concentration is the most important thing. It’s tough to play physically every three days, but it’s even tougher to constantly have this pressure of having to win.”

“I always expect this. He has the potential to do much more. He’s talented, like other players on the team. It’s no surprise, he’s very talented. It’s the mentality that counts.”

“We lost the ball without being pressured, trying to play the ball. We left Jashari alone to set up a team with four of our players behind their midfielders. When we had the ball, we gave it away without pressure.

“Koni sometimes put the ball in areas where there was pressure, but instead he was supposed to carry the ball. He’s responsible for pushing the team forward and guiding us forward. We went to get into their pressing zones.”

It’s your first comeback win of the season…

“I think it’s a great feeling. If you look at the Benfica match, we had several opportunities. We created more than today. You have to see it to believe it, and today we saw that we came from two goals behind and won 4-2. Our confidence will grow.”

#1384. Mauricio Pochettino is the new coach of Manchester United!

Who says international truce often means housekeeping… And on the Manchester United side, after a catastrophic start to the season, Michael Carrick left. After a particularly good second part of the 2025/2026 season, having taken over from Ruben Amorim and qualifying the Red Devils for the Champions League, the former midfielder obtained catastrophic results at the start of the year. The Mancuniens are thus in a sad eighteenth place in the Premier League standings and they quickly paid the price.

Very quickly, the name of Mauricio Pochettino appeared as the main candidate to replace him, ahead of other names like Eddie Howe or Julian Nagelsmann. The North American coach maintains a superb rating across the Channel, where he had obtained excellent results with Southampton, then at Tottenham between 2014 and 2019, including a Champions League final. If his return to London with Chelsea during the 2023/2024 season did not necessarily go very well, the former PSG coach remains considered a top coach by our English neighbors.

It was therefore quite natural that Manchester United turned to him, while the Argentinian had also had the ambition, for a long time, to coach the Red Devils one day. The Mancunians announced his arrival until 2029 via an official press release this Friday: “Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to take charge of the Manchester United men’s team from November 18. The club has reached an agreement with the United States Soccer Federation so that Mauricio and his staff can be released from their duties once their assignments with the United States men’s national team are completed. »

Note that they had to pay around nine million euros to snatch him from the United States selection, where he was under contract until 2030. The same for a good part of his staff. Pochettino will have a few days to discover his players – even if many are with their selection – and try to familiarize them with his methods before a huge meeting after the break: a shock against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday November 22. Baptism of fire for Pochettino therefore…

#1383. Neto set for first Juventus game since 2017 and says his Turin chapter was still open

Norberto Neto is set for his first competitive game in almost six months when Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League on Thursday night. Speaking on the eve of the match, the 37 year old goalkeeper said he still felt he had unfinished business in Turin.

Neto last played for Juventus in May 2017, when he was part of the side that beat Lazio 2-0 in the Coppa Italia final. More than nine years on, the Brazilian is in line to start again in black and white, with first choice Guglielmo Vicario being rested for the visit of the Cypriot side to the Allianz Stadium.

His most recent competitive outing came on 30 May with Botafogo, as Football Italia noted after Wednesday’s press conference. Since then he has been working as cover, a role he took on after joining as a free agent at the end of September.

Juventus moved for Neto after Kamil Grabara ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in training on 19 September, only days after keeping a clean sheet on his debut against NEC. The club confirmed his return on 28 September with a contract running until 30 June 2027.

Asked what drew him back, Neto explained that he had been looking for a next step that genuinely meant something to him. “Deep down, I felt my chapter with Juve was still open,” he said, in comments reported by ilBianconero, which carried the press conference live. He added that he is enjoying his work and is in Turin to help, whatever the coming months bring.

Opening the press conference, he described his feelings simply: “It’s hugely satisfying. I’m really excited to be back on the pitch, and proud to be part of this team.”

Neto was asked about Vicario, who is on loan from Tottenham and has been Luciano Spalletti’s regular choice in goal. He kept his answer short: “I don’t know how much my opinion matters, but he’s a top-level goalkeeper.”

The veteran also spoke warmly about the younger players around him. He said their eagerness to contribute was infectious and that the squad has the quality, will and determination it needs. On the goals Juventus have conceded this season, he pointed to a side that is still developing, with several players new to Serie A and finding their way. His own focus, he said, is on training at full intensity every day while the team looks for balance and consistency.

Juventus go into matchday five fifth in the league phase standings with ten points from four games. Omonia have won two and lost two. Neto warned against taking them lightly, saying they are a strong side who break forward with real quality, and revealed he knows their coach Fabiano from his years in Brazil.

He also stressed that Europe brings its own demands, noting that Juventus always carry a responsibility to compete to win in every tournament they enter.

Interest in the meeting was already strong after ticket sales for Omonia passed 35,000 last week. Next up in Serie A is the trip to Como, where both sides go in without suspensions.

For Neto, the night is a chance to add to the 22 appearances he made in his first spell, when he won two league titles, two Coppa Italia trophies and a Supercoppa Italiana as Gianluigi Buffon’s understudy.

#1382. Cisse claims he is ‘just getting back into it’ and responds to idea of 20-goal target

Alphadjo Cisse has praised head coach Ruben Amorim, and he insisted that he is ‘just getting back into it’ after his injury.

Things did not start well for Milan against Olympiacos as they fell two goals behind, something that they had already done on three occasions in the Europa League. A Lorenzo Pirola header (given as a Mike Maignan own-goal) and a Jota Silva strike put the hosts in command.

Then came 15 minutes of madness. Omari Hutchinson scored a lovely solo goal to get the Rossoneri back into it, then he set up both Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic to complete the turnaround, before Diego Moreira sealed the deal in the dying seconds.

Cisse spoke to the reporters in the mixed zone following the conclusion of the game to shed some light on what was another positive personal night in a winning effort, boosting the hopes of knockout round qualification. MilanNews relayed his words.

“We didn’t have a good first half. Coming back from half-time with a deficit wasn’t easy, but we had a good second half and we’re happy to have brought home these three points.”

“Scoring a goal is definitely always nice. I’m not happy with my performance today, but we’re taking home the goal and the victory. I could have done much better in the first half.”

⚽️ GOAL ALPHADJO CISSE! 😍 https://t.co/oJP512Cpn1

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 26, 2026

What was the morale like after their second goal and now at the end of the match?

“It’s never easy to be behind, but we have a strong team: turning things around isn’t easy, but it’s always nice. We’re continuing the work we’ve been doing.

“We’re very happy, let’s say we’ll be traveling a little more relaxed, but starting Monday we have another battle we need to win.”

“It’s November. But I’m still coming off a season where I was sidelined for four or five months, so let’s just say getting back into it, even though it’s November, isn’t easy. But I’m working towards it.”

“The Europa League is definitely a great competition. We’re a strong team and we hope to score even more.”

“No, I don’t have that target. Maybe I won’t tell you, we’ll see at the end of the season and take stock.”

“It’s great working with the coach and his staff. They help us a lot, we’re growing, and his work, let’s say, is coming through.”

Do you believe you’ll qualify? Are you more relaxed?

“No, definitely not relaxed. We believed in it even before this match and we have to believe in it again, and we also have other matches where we definitely need to get points.”

Have you unlocked headers in your repertoire?

“It’s something new, let’s just say I’ve never done it in the past. I might have scored one headed goal in my career, this year there are already two, and we’ll see.”

#1381. French team: the winners and losers of this November gathering

The November gathering was rich in lessons for the French team. With a victory against Turkey and a defeat against Italy, the Blues experienced two contrasting encounters, but ultimately achieved their objective by validating their qualification for the rest of the Nations League. This Sunday, the content left something to be desired, particularly on the defensive level and in the intensity of the pressing and which provoked the ire of Zinedine Zidane after the meeting. Obviously, several individuals scored points during this gathering, while others may have lost credit for the Blues’ upcoming games.

This gathering allowed several players to stand out and score points in the minds of the staff. This is particularly the case ofAndy Dioufwho took advantage of the playing time granted to show the extent of his qualities. Active on the left flank of the defense, the Inter Milan midfielder displayed great availability, with a real ability to project himself forward and support offensives. His activity in recovery, his investment in defensive work and his desire to play forward were also interesting. Everything was not perfect but in a position that was not very well provided, the Interist clearly showed that Zidane could count on him. Lucas Da Cunha is also one of the big winners of this gathering. After a good performance against Italy, the midfielder was particularly convincing against Turkey, delivering a successful match in midfield. Technically comfortable, he stood out for his quality of passing, his vision of the game and his ability to quickly find his partners in space.

Available, accurate in his transmissions and involved in defensive efforts, he displayed a particularly attractive face. For his second rally, Da Cunha has almost already established himself as an indisputable player in the midfield. Finally, Eli Junior Kroupiscorer against the Turks, is also one of the players who scored points during this international window. The young striker was able to take advantage of this experience with the Blues to get a little closer to the group and show his qualities. His offensive profile, his mobility and his willingness to provide solutions in the last meters constitute interesting arguments for the future. In a sector where competition is particularly high, each gathering represents an opportunity to stand out and gain credit with the staff. These three players took advantage of this period to send positive signals, with the hope of continuing this dynamic with a view to the Final 8 of the Nations League next March.

Among the successful firsts, we must necessarily mention Saël Kumbedi. A mystery guest on Zinédine Zidane’s list and summoned following Pierre Kalulu’s withdrawal, the former OL player was sharp for his first start this Sunday against Turkey. Not flamboyant, however, the Wolfsburg right-back showed that he was a credible candidate for the next gatherings even if the returns of Jules Koundé and Pierre Kalulu could obscure his international future in the long term. In any case, he scored points, unlike another player who we will talk about later, and showed that he can rejoin the group in the future in case of absences. In this line, Ibrahima Konate (re)applied to ZZ. Getting better and better with Real Madrid, the central defender was the author of a good rally and a reassuring tenure in central defense against Turkey. Despite increased competition from William Saliba, Dayot Upamecano, Maxence Lacroix and Jérémy Jacquet, the 27-year-old rock has shown that he is clearly fit to claim a place in the squad in the future.

And the happiness of Ibrahima Konaté causes the misfortune of Leny Yoro. While the numerous absences in defense could allow him to accumulate playing time and score points, the Manchester United defender ultimately did not play a single minute. The only outfield player in the group not to have played during this break, he could be the first fuse to blow with the returns of Lacroix and Saliba. Especially since Konaté seems to have taken a head start in the hierarchy. Yoro was therefore unable to seize the opportunity offered to him and could quickly see his chances of winning dwindle. On the other hand, the big loser of this gathering is undoubtedly Malo Gusto.

Wandered against Italy, the Chelsea full-back did not even have the opportunity to redeem himself against Turkey. Worse, Kumbedi’s encouraging tenure may suggest that the latter has now passed him in the hierarchy. A worrying situation for Gusto, who is already struggling to get playing time at club level with Chelsea. In front, Bradley Barcola didn’t score any points either. While he had a great opportunity to express himself with the absences of Désiré Doué and Ousmane Dembélé, the Parisian winger delivered two fairly average performances against Italy and Turkey. Interesting in sequences, he especially gave the impression of often being disconnected from his partners. Not to mention his finish and his last gesture are still frustrating. To hope to maintain an important place in the offensive hierarchy, he will have to show more regularity and influence, especially since Kroupi’s return from injury and promising debut could reshuffle the cards.

In the Lyonnais gang, Rayan Cherki is called to the stand. Even if he remains an important player in Zidane’s plans, the virtuoso must also remain vigilant. The Lyonnais has the full confidence of the coach and has once again demonstrated his ability to turn a match around thanks to his technical quality, by being involved in both goals against Turkey. But some of his choices and his body language can sometimes be annoying. His midfield positioning could also be called into question with the returns of Akliouche, Koné and Tchouaméni, especially if Zidane decides to reorganize his system. He nevertheless remains a real step ahead thanks to his valuable talent and his importance in offensive animation. Finally, in the goals, Robin Risser now appears officially relegated to third goalkeeper after Restes replaced Maignan against Turkey. A hierarchy which places him at the forefront among the players likely to leave the group if another goalkeeper were to perform and convince. In difficulty with RC Lens since the start of the season, the young Lensois goalkeeper, targeted by Bayern, will therefore have to remain efficient so as not to permanently lose his place at Clairefontaine.

#1380. Russell must do something wacky now after disappointing Bahrain GP qualifying

Never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher. It might even be worth setting your alarm for the 8am UK start time. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start in pole position for the first time this year. He will have Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton alongside him.

It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together. Throw in sweltering temperatures, low grip, high tyre degradation, and the ever-present threat of a Malaysian monsoon sweeping through Sepang, and you have the potential for fireworks.

Russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

Eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. He now trails his team mate nine-seven in qualifying head-to-head this year.“No to be honest,” Russell admitted when asked whether he knew why he was so slow. “This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac.“The lap times seven years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.”Mercedes’ lack of performance was doubly unexpected because not only did they arrive here with a massive upgrade package, but Russell revealed this week that he and Antonelli were foregoing the cooling vests you see some drivers sporting on the grid, in favour of car performance.

Toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian said. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”

Still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

At the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. It was a first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains, too. And with his long run pace looking more than decent, Verstappen should really hold on for his first win of 2026. Hamilton will do his best to hang on to the Dutchman’s coattails. The seven-time champion was delighted when told he had taken P2. “Let’s go guys! Finally! Great job guys, really great job. Car felt great.”

This was indeed an excellent performance from the Ferrari man – and just the tonic for the Scuderia after weeks of gossip and speculation. Hamilton was admittedly three tenths slower than his rival, which he put purely down to a power deficit on the straights, but he said he was hopeful his long run pace was more competitive. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

“It was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one change before qualifying and we hit the sweet spot,” he reflected afterwards. “I am so, so grateful. I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”

It is Russell, though, who needs a result even more badly if he is to remain a factor in the championship. “As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us,” he admitted, adding that “all the numbers” from the upgrade package suggested it was an improvement on the old car. “But I think there is going to be a lot happening tomorrow. The tyre deg is huge and race pace will be king. So even though today was a real disappointment it is not the be all and end all.”

No. 1 ☝️#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/01PqrckQS9

Tomorrow’s race will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will start on the front row together. It is a reasonable run down to turn one and there are overtaking opportunities through the first few corners at Sepang, with it being similar to the configuration in China, with plenty of lines and moves on offer.

Respect between two great champions 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/fbZ6aoKRyw

“Very difficult to understand. We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is the different to all the (other) tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi [Antonelli], made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”

On Kimi Antonelli’s track limits breach in Q2:

“Not good, because Q2 you know you are going to get through. You lose a set [of softs] in a qualifying that is so tight, where we are on the back foot. That is not good.”

Lewis Hamilton says this is the biggest crowd he has ever seen at Sepang, thanking the fans for making it here today. That is actually a bigger compliment than many watching at home may realise. The traffic this weekend has been horrendous. After 10 years without a race in Malaysia, during which time F1 has grown massively, I think they have forgotten how to do traffic management. Shuttles are inconsistent, taxis can’t get in/out, it’s taking forever just to reach the airport a few kilometres away - some fans have been braving the heat and walking. It took over two hours to get back into Kuala Lumpur last night (48km). My understanding is the Bahrainis are organising the race this year, while local forces are handling the traffic outside the circuit.

“The car has been very good since last week. It is good to come back [from his wrist injury] at such a time and I am enjoying it, fighting for the top three. Even though it was not my finest qualifying session it is a good feeling.

“It is a bit unfortunate we take a penalty on a track where we are that fast but, from eighth, I am confident we can come through the field and come back for a good result.”

“I love this energy [from the crowd]. Big, big thank you to Malaysia for welcoming us. It is so hot here. I keep saying it, but that has made it a massive challenge for the tyres, the car, the mechanics in the garage. I am really, really thankful to my team. We made so many changes through all these practice sessions. Because the cars are sliding, the tyres are overheating, it was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one last change going into qualifying and I think we hit the sweet spot. To be able to close the gap to two or three tenths to Max [Verstappen], who has been so quick all weekend, is great, and I am so grateful.

“I am much happier with where the car is, but tomorrow is a completely different ballgame. Making these tyres last around this track, they are overheating from the get-go. Every little bit of wheelspin you have, every little snap you have makes a difference of how far you are going to go. I like to think we have got a good balance. Max was really quick on his long runs, so I will just try my best to hold onto him tomorrow.”

A reminder that Isack Hadjar will drop from third to eighth after his grid penalty.

QUALIFYING CLASSIFICATIONCan't wait for Sunday! 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/qqi8hPDcKA

“It is fantastic. We have been trying many grand prix to get pole. Sometimes a bit closer than others but to finally get it, from where we started the season, pretty incredible. I am happy with today and, for sure, I am going to try and win tomorrow. When you start first, that is the target.”

Big disappointment that for Russell. After his win in Baku, where he said he finally felt hooked up to the car, he was desperate to build the momentum. P8, four places behind Antonelli, was not what he would have had in mind. Has it all to do in the race tomorrow.

Excellent (though not unexpected) pole for Verstappen, and a very good P2 for Hamilton. Could be some fireworks on the front row tomorrow.

*Hadjar’s three-place grid penalty will drop him down to eighth place for the race tomorrow.

Neither of the Red Bulls can improve in the first sector but it is those behind them who need significant improvements. The two Ferraris are going along nicely at the start of their final flying laps. Hadjar is unable to improve despite a purple final sector. Verstappen then goes fastest in the final sector and improves his advantage at the top.

Hamilton meanwhile went fastest in the middle sector and goes second fastest overall. Piastri cannot improve but stays ahead of Russell.

Norris is the final man across the line but is only fast enough for P6. That means that Verstappen takes pole in Malaysia, which is the first time this season that Red Bull have taken pole position. Hamilton is second with Hadjar third, although the Frenchman has a five-place grid penalty.

MAX VERSTAPPEN TAKES POLE FOR THE BAHRAIN GRAND PRIX IN MALAYSIA!! 👊#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/NgtaCAZacL

The two Red Bulls, who are one and two at the moment, will be the first two drivers across the line on these final efforts.

The other nine drivers in Q3 are in the pits so young Antonelli has the track to himself as he sets his one and only flying lap of Q3. He is over four tenths down on Verstappen through the first sector and has plenty of work to do.

The championship leader sets a decent middle sector where he loses no more time to Verstappen. As it stands he would put himself third before the others do their final runs. He comes across the line in P3 but will have the likes of Hamilton, Piastri, Leclerc, Norris and Russell trying to surpass him.

Russell is the first across the line and sets a time of a 1:36.032. He does not last long at the top as he is immediately displaced by Hadjar, who is half a second quicker.

Hamilton then comes over the line in second, just ahead of his teammate Leclerc. Piastri puts himself between the two Ferraris.

What about Verstappen? The man who won here the last time we were in Malaysia continues his great form today and goes quickest by more than three tenths.

Antonelli now heads out and will have the track to himself really. This is going to be the championship leader’s only flying lap of Q3.

Russell is the first man to head out for his first flying lap in Q3. Antonelli has remained in the pits with just one new set of softs remaining. Verstappen, who right now feels like the favourite for pole, will be one of the last across the line in these first attempts of Q3.

The fight for pole position in Sepang begins now as the green light is on at the end of the pit lane to get Q3 going.

Antonelli, due to that lap time deletion in Q2, has just one new set of softs for Q3, which could prove costly in his attempts to try and take pole.

P12 the best qualifying result of the season for Alonso. It was only his second time in Q2 after Hungary (P16).

I should add, P14 was also Lance Stroll’s best qualifying result of the season. His first outing in Q2 this year.

11. Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls)12. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin)13. Carlos Sainz (Williams)14. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls)

Verstappen, Leclerc, Piastri, Norris, Hadjar and Russell all remain in the pits. A bit of a risk for Russell down in eighth but his time should be enough to get into Q3.

Lindblad, who will start tomorrow’s race at the back of the grid after penalties, gives his teammate Lawson a tow down the back straight and it works as Lawson just sneaks into the top ten.

Can Bortoleto get back ahead though of Lawson? Yes he can and he will take the final place in Q3. Lawson thought he might be through but the tow was not enough.

Lindblad, who's taking a grid penalty for Sunday's race, gave team mate Lawson a tow but it wasn't quite enough to send the Kiwi into Q3#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/IMlrqg4ENv

As the young Italian starts his flying lap, there is no-one else out on track so no traffic. He is a lot more cautious at turn six this time than last time, when he had his lap time deleted.

He has not set blistering first and second sector times but a purple final sector puts him into second and the Italian is safely into Q3.

Plenty of other drivers are now heading around the track for their final flying laps of Q2.

11. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)12. Carlos Sainz (Williams)13. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes)14. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin)

Mercedes have put a brand new set of softs onto Antonelli’s car as he heads out promptly, with no lap time to his name so far. Antonelli is still disputing the lap deletion over team radio but his team tell him the images show he exceeded track limits. This is now a lot of pressure on the championship leader; any mistake now and he will not make Q3. His teammate Russell is only in seventh.

Antonelli was fourth fastest but has had his lap time deleted for exceeding track limits at turn six. That is a big moment in Q2 and could prove problematic if he gets into Q3. Antonelli appeared to be confused when he was told about his lap deletion over team radio but the on-board view looked pretty clear-cut.

Piastri then comes across the line in third.
