Verstappen has been shown a black and white flag for driving unnecessarily slowly. I doubt he will get a grid penalty for that but it will be a warning for the Dutchman.

Anyway, the drivers, other than Colapinto and Alonso, are on flying laps, with Verstappen currently fastest inthe first sector.

The green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and the second part of qualifying is under way. Like the start of Q1, it is hardly a stampede to go out.

17. Nico Hulkenberg (Audi)18. Oliver Bearman (Haas)19. Esteban Ocon (Haas)20. Alex Albon (Williams)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac)

The Aston Martin of Stroll improves significantly from 20th and is set to make Q2, as is his teammate Alonso. A bit of a surprise to see the Aston Martins improve and make it into Q2.

Go Fernando! 🤩 Go Lance! 🤩First double Q2 appearance this season 🙌#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/xjiWYv6ycr

That has seen the Audi of Hulkenberg drop into the drop zone and the German is out. For contrast, his teammate improves to go into eighth place! Hulkenberg had a big lock up into turn 14, which proved very costly.

As it stands, eight of the top nine are remaining in the garage. Russell is in ninth and has not gone out but Gasly above him in eighth has. You would imagine Russell is perfectly safe.

17. Esteban Ocon (Haas)18. Alex Albon (Williams)19. Oliver Bearman (Haas)20. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac)

Ocon, in 17th, is quite far off Hulkenberg in 16th and needs more than four tenths to usurp him.

The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he says Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

It’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

“Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he said. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

He added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”

The two Ferraris are on medium tyres but Leclerc still puts himself into second place. He is then displaced by Hamilton, who slots in behind Verstappen. Good times from the Ferraris on the mediums.

What about the McLarens? Norris goes sixth fastest but is more than six tenths down on Verstappen. Then comes Piastri, who goes fourth fastest, just under four tenths off Verstappen.

Arguably the three favourites for pole; Antonelli, Russell and Verstappen, are all on flying laps.

The first sector goes the way of Verstappen, who is purple, and then the Dutchman goes purple in the middle sector.

Antonelli is two tenths faster than his teammate Russell but Verstappen is over half a second quicker than the Mercedes. Hadjar is then second fastest to show the pace in the Red Bull this weekend.

Most of the teams waited and waited to come out and then suddenly lots of drivers are sent out, resulting in a queue in the pits! With the high track temperatures and high degradation, the drivers are crawling around on their out laps to preserve these soft tyres.

Bumper to bumper in the pit lane! #F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/ff8JO9kB1g

The two Haas drivers have a free track to themselves whilst everyone else bides their time. In theory, as the hour of qualifying goes on, the track temperature should decrease and the more rubber that is laid down the faster the track should get.

Finally, just before the two Haas drivers finish their first flying laps, the rest of the grid is starting to emerge, led by the Mercedes duo.

The green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and Q1 is officially under way. The two Haas drivers are the first to head out. Other than that, it is a quiet start to Q1.

The top four teams; Mercedes, Red Bull, Ferrari and McLaren, all have a genuine chance of taking pole in Sepang today. I think the true favourites though have to be the Mercedes duo and Max Verstappen but with how close it between all four of the teams you cannot rule anything out.

It is 33 degrees celsius air temperature, with the track temperature up at 58 degrees.

Not long to wait now until qualifying begins. It is hot, humid and dry in Sepang right now. As we know in Malaysia, the weather can change quickly and thunderstorms can roll in quite quickly but it looks like today’s qualifying will be a dry one. This will be one of if not the hottest qualifying sessions of the season, so much so that we are seeing umbrellas going up to get some shade from the sun rather than sheltering from any rain.

This will be important to consider after qualifying finishes as there will be some shuffling around:

Isack Hadjar (Red Bull): five-place grid penalty- new internal combustion engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): ten-place grid penalty- new engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): five-place grid penalty- causing a collision in BakuArvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls): back of the grid- complete power unit change

Hadjar has looked good since returning from his wrist injury so could be fighting it out near the front of the grid, although his five-place penalty will drop him down. We know Lindblad will be at the back and is very likely to be joined there by Colapinto, who is not going to be qualifying high up in the top ten in his Alpine.

Haas have announced that Frenchman Esteban Ocon will leave at the end of this season. Ocon now faces an uncertain future, with it difficult to see a spot for him on the F1 grid next season. There are suggestions that the 30-year-old’s replacement will be Brazilian Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, although nothing has been confirmed on that front. 21-year-old Camara currently leads the Formula 2 championship.

TGR Haas F1 Team and Esteban Ocon will part ways at the conclusion of the 2026 season. With plenty of racing ahead, our focus remains on working together to maximize every opportunity through to the final race of the year.#HaasF1 #F1 pic.twitter.com/4iQAuqnSyA

Aston Martin have now confirmed their driver line-up for next season, retaining both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll. There had been reports that Alonso had been contemplating retirement but the 45-year-old will continue into another season.

Aston Martin Aramco confirms Lance and Fernando will continue as the team's drivers in 2027. Read more: ​https://t.co/ePyjJdyAIB pic.twitter.com/VogFUEbNxy

Other than the second seat alongside Ollie Bearman at Haas, the only other team to keep an eye on is Racing Bulls, with no definite confirmation on their exact driver line-up for next season.

Ferrari this week have publicly backed their team principal Frederic Vasseur, amid speculation over the Frenchman’s position and comments made by former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner, who said the job at Ferrari would be a “dream job”. Ferrari, who sit second in the constructors’ standings, have not won the drivers’ championship since 2007 (Kimi Raikkonen) and the constructors’ since 2008. Here is a snippet from Tom Cary’s piece on the matter:

In a hastily convened media call on Tuesday morning, Maria Conti, Ferrari’s chief communication officer, said the Scuderia had decided to issue a vote of confidence in Vasseur in response “not just to the story of Mr Horner, but in general, the speculation about Fred”.

“Ferrari has made its choices,” Conti said. “We have confidence – full confidence – in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so.

“At this time, it’s really important that the team remains united and cohesive, and we are focused with all the energy on the work ahead.”

“It is great to be back [in Malaysia]. I am really enjoying the track. We have had some wonderful races here over time. It is actually the 20th time we have been here, it started in 1999, and it is really exciting to be back. I really enjoyed getting out on the track and watching the cars closely.

“The drivers are super fit and they have some cooling but it is not easy. But you almost cannot get enough fluid through your body before your stomach gives up. Having this race and Singapore back-to-back increases that challenge.”

Especially with the big upgrade they have brought this weekend, Mercedes’ lead at the summit is looking unassailable right now.

Almost nine years ago to the day, Max Verstappen took just his second race victory in Formula 1. Lewis Hamilton, who took pole position, and Daniel Ricciardo joined Verstappen on the podium. Despite being nine years ago, plenty of drivers still on the grid were racing that weekend. Here they are and who they were racing for:

Max Verstappen (Red Bull) Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes) Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes) Esteban Ocon (Force India)Nico Hulkenberg (Renault)Sergio Perez (Force India)Fernando Alonso (McLaren)Lance Stroll (Williams)Carlos Sainz (Toro Rosso)Pierre Gasly (Toro Rosso)

With Russell winning in Baku and Antonelli finishing fifth, the latter’s championship lead was cut to 66 points. If Russell is going to usurp his teammate, he is going to need a few more similar results to last weekend due to the size of Antonelli’s lead. If Antonelli were to suffer a retirement, then that completely changes the outlook.

Formula One returns to Malaysia for round 16 of the season for the Bahrain Grand Prix. That probably sounds strange but after the Bahrain Grand Prix was originally postponed in March, F1 reinstated it to the calendar with Malaysia hosting it because of the ongoing war in the Middle East. Despite being held in Malaysia, Bahrain have retained the naming rights for the event, which is officially known as the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The last time Formula One was in Malaysia was nine years ago back in 2017, when a young whippersnapper named Max Verstappen, still four years away from winning his first world championship, claimed just his second victory.

Last time out around the streets of Baku, Mercedes’ George Russell claimed victory at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, pipping Verstappen by just a tenth of a second. That was Russell’s first grand prix win since June and cuts his team-mate Kimi Antonelli’s lead in the drivers’ standings to 66 points. Antonelli had a challenging weekend in Baku, starting 16th after a crash in qualifying and coming home in fifth to see his championship lead to Russell cut by 15 points.

Verstappen was quickest in first practice yesterday, with the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc fastest in second practice. Earlier today, championship leader Antonelli was nearly three tenths clear of the field in third practice. Mercedes, 160 points clear at the top of the constructors’ standings, have brought significant upgrades this weekend, which includes a new floor, rear suspension and rear corner. It is the team’s first significant car update since the Canadian Grand at the end of May.

This race in Malaysia represents the second leg of the season’s first flyaway triple header, with the Singapore Grand Prix to come next weekend, so the demands on the teams and the drivers are incredibly high. Qualifying from Sepang gets under way at 9am (GMT).

#1379. PSG: the impressive rise of Titis in the national selection

PSG sees several of its young talents joining the national teams this November. The capital club is particularly well represented in the different youth categories of the France team, with Dimitri Lucea and Quentin Ndjantou called up with the U20s, Lucas Batbedat and David Boly with the U19s, while five Parisians appear on the U17 list. Mamadou Meïté, Noha Tiehi and Seydou Konaté were also called up with the U18s for the U17 World Cup in Qatar. Note that Senny Mayulu was finally promoted to A after several injuries in the French team.

This Parisian presence goes beyond French borders. Léo Gnahoré will defend the colors of Côte d’Ivoire U18, while Adam Mouak joined Morocco U18 for the Qatari World Cup. Dro Fernandez is called up with Spain U19 and Alessandro Longoni with Italy U19, even if the latter had to leave the gathering after being injured. A great showcase for the Parisian team, which sees several of its young players continuing their progress on the international scene.

#1378. Roma draw 2-2 at PSG as Malen’s late penalty adds to Juventus’ December challenge

Roma came from behind to draw 2-2 with holders Paris Saint-Germain, with substitute Donyell Malen scoring a 78th-minute penalty. The leaders' rivals above Juventus showed the depth of their squad less than a month before they host Spalletti's side.

Roma left the Parc des Princes with a point and with their reputation enhanced. Mario Hermoso gave them the lead against the European champions. Paris Saint-Germain turned the game around through an Illia Zabarnyi header and an Ousmane Dembélé penalty.

In Europe, Malen’s spot-kick was his fifth goal. Across all competitions, it marked his 17th strike of the campaign, from 16 appearances. It came days after he scored four times in Roma’s 5-1 win at Parma. Yet he did not start in Paris, and neither did Paulo Dybala. Gian Piero Gasperini said he left Malen out because of the number of games he had played for Roma and the Netherlands.

That a reshuffled Roma could take a point in Paris says plenty about their squad. Luis Enrique’s side had not dropped points since a home defeat to Monaco on 4 September.

The result does not fix Roma’s European position. The club lists the game as Matchday 5 of the league phase. Roma have one win, two draws and two defeats so far. Under the format, clubs finishing 9th to 24th enter the play-offs, while 25th to 36th are knocked out. The top eight go straight into the round of 16.

That leaves Roma with work to do in a crowded December. Their next Champions League match is at home to Sporting CP on 8 December, kicking off at 21:00. They then travel to AEK Athens on 19 January and host Lille on 27 January 2027.

Domestically, Roma’s form has been strong. Their league record shows nine wins and three draws, with 36 goals scored and 11 conceded, Corriere dello Sport reported.

For Spalletti’s side, the schedule offers some contrast. After that European fixture, Roma play the derby away to Lazio on Sunday 13 December at 12:30. That leaves them six days between the derby and the visit of Juventus. Before travelling to Rome, Juventus are away to Como on 29 November. Udinese and Monza then come to Turin in Serie A, on 6 December and 14 December respectively.

Whether Roma’s European commitments take a toll remains to be seen. The evidence from Paris suggests Gasperini can rotate without a sharp drop in quality. Malen’s form, from the bench or from the start, will be a central concern for Juventus.

The two sides meet in round 16 of Serie A on Saturday 19 December 2026, with kick-off at 20:45.

#1375. Bayern Munich fully accepts its inappropriate comments about Jamal Musiala

Absent from the field since September 18 and the match against Union Berlin (7-0), Jamal Musiala made his return this weekend against Cologne (1-1), a match in which he played 20 minutes. Affected by a serious neurological health problem, the young 23-year-old German attacking midfielder is at the heart of a huge controversy across the Rhine. The reason? The management of Bayern Munich speaks (too) openly about the health concerns of its player, without really taking into account the traditional medical confidentiality so often respected in the world of football. Recently, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge even went a little further by discussing the financial aspect of the affair.

“What we know suggests that it will be difficult to reach the level he has so often displayed here. We need to talk to the family, the player and especially his representatives. These sums are no longer possible – sorry, with all due respect. » Words that shocked an entire country, as well as FIFPro. The international players’ union issued a statement ordering Bayern to respect their player. And if Bayern speaks this way about the Musiala case, it is because the German international (46 caps, 10 goals) has a contract until 2030 paid at the rate of €25 million gross per season. Suffice it to say that the Bavarian management fears more than ever having to pay so much every month for a player who could never again find his former level, even if it means causing an outcry.

Faced with the controversy, one of the bosses of Bayern, Jan-Christian Dreesen, spoke in the columns of Bild. “Everything has already been said about Musiala. We must now take care of him and let him play. I was delighted that he was on the field on Friday as planned. We now hope that it will return to its former form. The fans are concerned about this situation because each of our players is one of us. Jamal is one of us! This is precisely why we watch over him. So it was obvious that there would be a reaction. But to be honest, I was simply surprised by the reaction of FIFPro. This players association is not even represented in Germany »he confided, before continuing:

“I maintain my position: it is our duty to ensure that Jamal has time to recover and return to his former levels. At the same time, we also have a responsibility towards the club. Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge made the same comments, even if they phrased them differently. And I think that’s a very valid argument. (…) If I may say so, the discussion around our “Mia San Mia” (motto which notably advocates unity within the club, editor’s note) seems a little forced to me. No one said we weren’t taking care of Jamal and doing everything we could to support him. But everything has already been said on the subject, and we should focus on taking care of him, instead of just talking. (…) Winter is just beginning and it will be long. I don’t think we should set a specific number of weeks for his return. We will assess the situation in a few months and take stock. Jamal’s situation is the same as any other player who has been out for two months. He needs time to come back. » Continued in the next episode.

#1373. Real Madrid just received a crazy offer for Endrick!

The winter transfer window should be rather calm on the Castellana side. After a somewhat sluggish start to the season, which earned early criticism from Mourinho and a good number of players in the squad, the Merengues found their cruising speed and caught up with Barça in La Liga, in addition to achieving a perfect run in the Champions League. Everything seems to be going well, and, a priori, no need to strengthen this winter.

The Merengue leaders are not very fond of winter recruitment in any case. On the other hand, in terms of departures, there could be movement, with players who could leave on loan, like the young Thiago Pitarch, barred by competition in midfield. But if there’s one name that’s going to be talked about in January, it’s Endrick. It is difficult, at present, to know the player’s plans. What is certain is that he does not seem to totally matter to José Mourinho, who has only started him once this season (for 8 TCC appearances in total).

A difficult situation for a player who needs playing time to continue his progress. Especially since there is no shortage of suitors, with a good number of Premier League and Serie A clubs dreaming of welcoming him. It is AC Milan which seems the hottest on the file, and the Cadena SER has just confirmed the interest of the Lombards in the 20-year-old striker. Better, the media indicates that an offer of 70 million euros has already been made, and that it has therefore already arrived on the desk of the management of Real Madrid. AC Milan have even already spoken with Endrick to express their interest.

For the moment, José Mourinho does not wish to part ways with the player. For his part, Endrick is not necessarily leaning towards leaving but the former Palmeiras’ entourage could push him to pack his bags. In the event that a transfer is not possible this winter, the Milanese team has already planned to go on the attack again this summer. A sign that Ruben Amorim and the Milanese decision-makers are really counting on him. On the Merengue side, we would even make a small added value on the player, who had cost 35 million euros fixed + 25 million euros in the form of bonuses which have not yet been reached. To be continued…

#1372. Wesley reveals: “I told Endrick to come to Roma. He would be given a special welcome”

Roma, fresh from a 2-2 draw at PSG in the Champions League, are looking for a striker to bolster Gasperini’s attack.

Among the most closely watched prospects is Real Madrid’s Endrick.

Wesley, his compatriot, admitted to TNT Sports that he wants to play with him in the capital.

“I told Endrick to come and play for Roma! He’ll decide his future; obviously, it’s his career… I hope that wherever he goes, or if he stays at Real Madrid, he’ll be very happy and successful, because he’s a good guy who deserves it.”

“But if he comes, he’ll be very well received by the Roma fans and by us, of course.”

#1371. The numbers behind Hermoso’s monster performance vs PSG

Mario Hermoso was Roma’s man of the match at PSG.

The Spanish center-back never feared the team that has won the last two Champions Leagues and scored the goal that temporarily led 0-1.

The former Atlético Madrid player delivered a performance worthy of a total leader: high recoveries, intercepted balls, quality with the ball at his feet, and constant support for the attack, even finding himself consistently in the French team’s penalty area.

Hermoso, after the match, commented with a hint of bitterness on the 2-2 draw against PSG: “An important point. It’s a shame not to take home three points, but one is good. We want to fight for everything, we have the mentality to do so, and we also have the quality.”

Roma fans have fallen in love with Mario Hermoso. In a very tough match, the Spanish defender showcased his leadership skills with a near-perfect performance.

As reported by Corriere dello Sport, the 1995-born defender won 11 possessions, won 6 duels, and took 5 shots, 4 of which were from inside the opponent’s penalty area. A complete player.

#1370. Tom Heaton breaks the fourth wall with priceless reaction to Man Utd’s post-match weights

Tom Heaton’s smile said a lot about Manchester United’s decision to do post-match weight training on the side of the pitch and in the view of the media.

Manchester United drew 2-2 away at Sporting in a game filled with incident. Three penalties, one red card, a goalkeeper howler and a horrendous pitch-enforced bobble means that Mauricio Pochettino will have to wait until his third game at least for his first win in charge.

A lot of the talk surrounding Pochettino’s arrival at Old Trafford is that the players better be ready to work hard and so what better way to demonstrate that work than by having the players perform a weight routine on the side of the pitch where all the cameras can see them.

The TNT cameras were on hand to capture the United players doing weight routines on the side of the pitch with Shea Lacey front and centre.

One player who looked slightly bemused as to why this was happening is third-choice goalkeeper Tom Heaton.

The 40-year-old, who has been around the block a few times, gave a cheeky look towards the cameras as if to say “yes, we are doing performative weight training on the side of the pitch.”

All of this is part of Project Pochettino which aims to turn the unbothered United squad into one of the hardest-working in the Premier League.

But he will want to start winning games as soon as possible and suggested they should have on Wednesday night.

“I think we dominated and we deserved to win the game, but we didn’t for different circumstances,” he said.

“All the teams make mistakes, but for these mistakes the punishment is too big in every single mistake. Many other clubs make mistakes or tilt in a different circumstance, in a more positive way. But that is in the way we are. We need to take responsibility.”

READ: The 11 Man Utd players out on loan in 2026-27 & how they’ve been faring

Pochettino may also have a problem in goal after Senne Lammens, who at one point in his United career looked like a much-needed safe pair of hands, spilt an easy catch for Sporting’s second.

Pochettino, though, defended his player and said these things happen.

“This type of thing happens,” he said. “That is football. Football is about making mistakes.

“I always want to support my player. I think we need to talk about responsibility. In this type of action our defensive line needs to cover the keeper better because it was very difficult.

“It’s not to blame the defensive line, but it’s two things that we need to improve, details that we need to work on. We need to manage this type of situation better.”

#1369. Gasperini’s Roma earns the respect of the football world

Gasperini’s Roma showed off their true essence to the football world, and they did so on a Champions League night away to Paris Saint-Germain, European champions for the past two seasons.

There was no better stage to gain confidence in their abilities and earn the respect of the giants of the game. PSG was coming off a 12-match winning streak against: Slovan Bratislava (6-1), Brest (0-1), Marseille (1-2), Le Mans (3-1), Manchester City (2-4), Strasbourg (1-3), Barcelona (4-2), Lyon (2-0), Le Havre (1-5), Villareal (0-6), Troyes (1-0), and Nice (2-3).

Then came Gasperini’s Roma, who, after just five minutes, rocked the Parc des Princes with Mario Hermoso’s lead.

The match ended 2-2, but the Giallorossi may have some regrets, given that the Spanish center-back had chances to give his team the three points, even in the final minutes. “We were used to winning, then Roma came along,” Joao Neves bitterly commented.

Gasperini’s Roma gave the giants a run for their money, the strongest team in the world, which, despite the absences of Kvaratskhelia and Doue, remains among the best teams around.

The highest praise came from PSG members themselves, who acknowledged Roma’s strength: “These are the teams we enjoy playing against and competing against. I think it’s precisely games like this that allow us to grow, learn, and gain experience in this competition.”

Joao Neves was clear: the Giallorossi are a great team to face, a team that has won the last two Champions League titles and this year thrashed record-breaking Barcelona 4-2, currently leading La Liga. A remarkable demonstration of respect.

Luis Enrique went further: “It’s clearly the most difficult match of the season against a Roma side whose quality we know. It was very tough, so I congratulate Roma. We could have lost, without a doubt. I see a bright future for them and I think they can win the Scudetto; it wouldn’t surprise me.” Gasperini’s team is working to become a major force in Italy and Europe: they passed the toughest test at the Parc des Princes with flying colors. They’re on the right path, Gasperini promises.

#1368. Soule shines: 10 goal contributions in 17 matches

It wasn’t Hercules, but Matias Soulé who lit up the Parc des Princes.

The Argentine talent took just five minutes to become the star of yet another great European night: a decisive assist for Hermoso after dancing to the ball, skipping past opponents.

Gian Piero Gasperini expressed his satisfaction at seeing a player continually improving: “Besides being strong, he’s very positive, he’s receptive, and he wants to grow. He’s 23, and he’s in a period where he can grow, as he is doing. He’s more complete than before; today he’s played on the left, whereas until last year he was stuck on that pitch. He’s reaching extraordinary technical and physical maturity. I’m happy for him; in these last two months, he’s been doing something very positive.”

Matias Soulé shows no signs of slowing down his unstoppable growth. The Argentine winger has already been involved in 10 goals this season, one every 114 minutes: four goals and six assists in 17 appearances.

The Argentine talent’s performances this year are rising in proportion to the quality of his opponents: he has rarely been without a hand in big matches.

In fact, Soulé scored one goal and provided three assists in the Champions League matches against Real Madrid, Manchester United, and PSG.

In the league, he was instrumental with a goal that allowed Roma to a last-gasp 2-1 victory against Atalanta, adding to his assist for Hermoso that temporarily tied the game 1-1. On October 24, he lit up the Maradona stadium with a total performance from start to finish, further enhanced by the goal that sparked the comeback to secure a 3-3 draw at Napoli.

#1367. The story of Eric Cantona and his incredible impact on Man Utd

On May 17, 1997, Eric Cantona announced his retirement from football. He was only 30 years old, but his impact on Manchester United and on English football had been immeasurable.

“‘Ooh ahh, Cantona’? They won’t sing it here.”

That was one of the more extreme responses from a supporter outside Old Trafford (see video below) the day after Cantona stunned football – not for the first time and certainly not for the last – by signing for Manchester United.

As a 12-year-old red growing up in a Leeds United heartland, I certainly wasn’t sure how to process the breaking story late in the Calendar News bulletin at 6.25pm on Thursday, November 26, 1992.

Cantona had played a significant part in my misery up to that point, and his chant had provided the backing music for some merciless stick at school six months earlier when he helped Leeds deny my team their first Championship in 25 years. Yet here he was, switching sides.

Alex Ferguson did little to reassure his club’s supporters that there was method to the madness when he admitted Cantona only came into his mind “more or less” when Leeds called to enquire about Denis Irwin.

Cantona had only joined Leeds in January, signed for £900,000 by Howard Wilkinson from Nimes, and though the then-24-year-old made only six starts and another nine appearances off the bench in the second half of that 1991-92 season, his cameos helped Leeds beat Ferguson’s men to the title.

Cantona’s three goals came at home against teams in the lower half of the table, but he got the ball rolling against Luton and Wimbledon and broke Chelsea’s resistance with one of the goals of the season.

With Cantona, Leeds took 13 points from their final five games of the run-in, while Man Utd drew one and lost three on the spin against Nottingham Forest, West Ham and Liverpool to almost gift-wrap the final pre-Premier League title for their Yorkshire rivals.

Though Ferguson acknowledged in both autobiographies that Leeds were worthy champions, his side unquestionably blew it as his fear over the goals drying up became a reality.

Coincidence though it may be, when Leeds signed Cantona, Man Utd were averaging 2.9 goals per game over 26 matches. In the final 16-game run-in, that plummeted to one goal per game, while they were shut out six times.

Sixteen games into the following campaign, United were eighth and again averaging only a goal per game when a call took place which changed the face of English football.

“I remember that phone call clearly, as though it was yesterday,” Leeds’ former Managing director Bill Fotherby said in 2012.

“We agreed to pay Eric something like £500,000 if we kept him after the initial period of six months. It was an immense amount of money for Leeds, but we agreed to it because we had this recommendation from Michel Platini and we judged the most important thing was to get the player.

“We wanted to do whatever it took and deal with the rest afterwards. But there were difficulties almost immediately.

“Apart from Lee Chapman, no-one in the squad spoke fluent French, and for Howard, it was a bit of a nightmare. Although we had won the title, there was just no connection between the two and, in the end, he told me to try and find Eric another club.

“Howard Wilkinson was an absolute perfectionist. He wanted his players to be disciplined and adhere to a certain team pattern. Eric just didn’t fit it.

While Cantona might not have been suited to Leeds, he found his perfect match across the Pennines.

“If ever there was one player, anywhere in the word, that was made for Manchester United, it was Cantona,” said Ferguson later.

“He swaggered in, stuck his chest out, raised his head and surveyed everything as though he were asking: ‘I’m Cantona. How big are you? Are you big enough for me?’”

Ince, the self-styled Guvnor, said Cantona “took the responsibility away from us lot”, which was evident from the manner in which United attacked the second half of the season.

They doubled their goals per game over the remaining 26 matches, netting 50 times in 18 wins, losing only twice on their way to breaking a 26-year title drought. Famine was about to become feast.

Ferguson had been searching for a goalscorer, but in Cantona he found something rarer. The Frenchman notched nine goals over the remainder of the season, perhaps not a Shearer-esque strike-rate, but he offered 11 assists.

More than anything tangible, Cantona brought a swagger and a confidence which often strutted over the border to an arrogance that so inspired his team-mates and wowed fans at the now Stretford End-less Old Trafford.

With Bryan Robson’s powers waning, Cantona arrived at the perfect time. Countless team-mates have referenced how the Frenchman became the example to follow at The Cliff. They had a new leader.

Even Ferguson admits Cantona “opened my eyes to the indispensability of practice”.

With Cantona leading the line, United felt and often looked invincible. The burden of responsibility Ince referred to was gone, and they followed up the title in 1993 with their first-ever Double in 1994.

Cantona, with his collar up, was at the heart of all that the purists identified as good and bad about that 93-94 team. He scored 25 goals in all competitions and contributed 13 assists, earning himself the PFA Player of the Year award.

There was no sign of the temper United had been warned about until the Champions League trip to Galatasaray in November 1993 when Cantona received his first red card in a United shirt for insulting the referee, who he later accused of being “bought”.

As he and his team-mates descended down the steps towards the underground changing rooms, Cantona was slyly attacked by a baton and shield-wielding policeman, as was Robson when the skipper rushed to defend his team-mate.

“In the dressing room, Eric went crazy,” Roy Keane recalled in his autobiography. “While the rest of us just wanted to get out of there, Eric was determined to sort out the rogue cop who had been wielding his truncheon.

“Eric was a big, strong lad. He was serious. He insisted he was going to kill that f***er. It took the combined efforts of the manager, Brian Kidd and a few of the players to restrain him.”

Much like supporters, Cantona’s blood boiled at the thought of any perceived injustice, and that connection made it easy for United fans to not only forgive Eric’s misdemeanours but to revel in them.

Cantona simmered over later that season when he was banned for five games after red cards in successive draws at Swindon and Arsenal. But those incidents were merely child’s play compared to what was to come at Crystal Palace the following season.

The kung-fu kick on Matthew Simmons was the release of 48 minutes of frustration after Cantona had felt he had been kicked around Selhurst Park without any protection from Alan Wilkie.

Cantona questioned the referee at half-time while, according to Wilkie, Ferguson was more direct: “Why don’t you do your f*cking job!”

Three minutes after emerging from the tunnel for the second half, Cantona was being directed back towards it after dishing out his own form of justice to his shadow for the night, Richard Shaw.

Ferguson says he has “never been able to elicit an explanation from Eric” as to why he felt the need to react to Matthew Simmons that way. Unsurprisingly, it seems he did it because he felt like it.

“Millions of times people say these things, and then one day you don’t accept it,” Cantona said.

“Why? It’s not about words. It’s about how you feel at that moment. One day you react, but the words are exactly the same as those you have heard a million times, so it is impossible to say why you react.”

Cantona was subsequently suspended for nine months by the FA, and United went on to miss out on the title by a single point to Blackburn before losing the FA Cup final to Everton a week later.

To make matters worse, the FA threatened to extend Cantona’s suspension because he had been photographed taking part in a friendly against Rochdale that was nothing more than a behind-closed-doors kickabout of three thirds.

Cantona reacted by submitting a transfer request in early August.

Inter Milan, who were at Selhurst Park on that night in January to scout Cantona, would have been delighted to offer him a haven in Italy, but Ferguson travelled to Paris to convince his star player to stay put.

He later described that journey as “one of the more worthwhile acts I have performed in this stupid job of mine”.

Given the success that followed, that must rate as one of Ferguson’s greatest understatements. Another Double, this time with kids, and an additional Premier League title after that certainly justified his decision to smooth the path back for Cantona.

Cantona’s critics question his record, especially in European competition – though a goal every other game over six seasons and an assist for every three of his 185 appearances certainly stands up to scrutiny.

But Cantona’s contribution cannot be assessed by numbers.

United fans remember the moments. The good ones were incredible, and even the bad ones were great.

Important goals, like the volley at Newcastle to break Kevin Keegan’s heart or the retreating shot from the edge of the box to win the 1996 FA Cup final against Liverpool’s Spice Boys.

And great goals too, against Sunderland or an even better lob in a gale at Sheffield United.

Eric Cantona vs Sheffield United, 1995. pic.twitter.com/CukcNEykQm

— 90s Football (@90sfootball) June 27, 2020

In terms of technique, Cantona was the best Old Trafford had seen for some time, but with regard to charisma, he was perhaps the greatest ever.

Robson will always be revered – despite not being a United product, he was the Stretford End’s representative on the pitch. Work hard, play hard, tackle harder, Captain Marvel was easy to relate to, but Eric was an enigma as well as an icon.

Never misunderstood at Old Trafford but being barely understood by his public certainly added to the mercurial Frenchman’s charm.

Like many of us were told about Best, Law and Charlton, there is now a generation of supporters who were never lucky enough to experience Cantona first-hand, and no amount of YouTube highlights videos can make those poor souls feel what Eric made United fans feel in the 1990s.

#1366. PSG’s Nuno Mendes applauds Roma: “They’ve been one of the hardest teams we played this year.”

Nuno Mendes acknowledged the difficulties Paris Saint-Germain faced in their 2-2 draw against Roma at the Parc des Princes.

The Portuguese full-back, playing in the mixed zone, praised the tactical work of Gian Piero Gasperini’s team, which caused considerable difficulty for the French and European champions with intense pressing and precise organization.

“There are teams that will try to play this way in the future, and we’ll be ready. We already know what we have to do for the full 90 minutes. They caused our team a lot of problems, but I think we managed to overcome their pressure at times.”

“There were also moments when they managed to find space, win the ball back, and cause us problems. They were one of the most difficult teams to face. We have our own way of playing, and we never change. They analyzed it carefully, just as we had studied Roma, but they still managed to create a lot of problems for us. There are games where we can’t always be at our best, but we’ll keep trying.”

#1365. Valencia open talks with Dovbyk’s entourage

Artem Dovbyk also watched Bologna’s last match from the bench.

The Ukrainian attacker is still waiting for his first start for the Felsinei; first Tedesco and then Palladino aren’t impressed by the former Girona player. Quite the opposite.

The 1997-born player moved to the Rossoblu on loan this summer with an option to buy for €17 million, an option that will never be exercised and forces Roma to take direct interest, to avoid further devaluing a €41 million investment.

Now Valencia are serious and considering signing Dovbyk. One of the issues to be resolved is his €3 million net salary, of which €2.5 million is paid by the Rossoblu. The Spanish club is expected to pay half.

According to Il Resto del Carlino, recent news has revealed direct contact between the Spanish club and the Ukrainian player, who has reportedly expressed interest in a return to La Liga.

The 1997-born player has left a lasting impression, having scored 24 goals for Girona. Valencia has initiated initial discussions with Roma to understand potential terms and costs: approval will be needed from Bologna, which will pay Dovbyk €2.5 million of his €3 million net salary.

#1364. Michael Carrick’s farewell message to Manchester United

It’s now official. Fired by Manchester United, Michael Carrick was replaced by Mauricio Pochettino at the head of the Red Devils. A classic fuse after the catastrophic start to the season for the Mancunians (18th in the Premier League standings), the 45-year-old former midfielder leaves without bitterness. He also posted a long farewell message to the English club and its supporters on his Instagram account.

“Dear Manchester United supporters, I have had the immense privilege of managing Manchester United, the football club that I love. Few people have the chance to experience this and feel its full impact, and I am infinitely grateful. With that comes immense responsibility, and to be part of Manchester United you have to understand exactly what that entails. It’s different from any other place. In the end, you have to give your all to be the best, but there is a culture, values ​​and behaviors that you must adhere to and respect, and which have been built over time. They are a unique football club with substance and history that cannot be ignored. This is what inspired me every day. I would like to send a huge thank you to the supporters. I must say that you are exceptional people, a rare breed. We had some great moments this year, moments that we will all remember. The best part of my job is seeing so many of you let yourself be carried away by the emotion of these moments, leaving the stadium with the irrepressible desire to come back next time. I just wanted to return some of that love. This love never dies. I know the results haven’t been there lately, but you’ve shown me nothing but love and support at times when the easier solution, and the one most end up choosing, would have been to turn away. It matters more than just one or two wins. It’s what makes you who you are. This is why I fell in love with this club so many years ago. A special thank you to my technical staff. You gave me everything you had, day after day, and I couldn’t have asked for more. I am infinitely grateful to you for your loyalty, hard work and support throughout this journey. To all the staff behind the scenes, thank you for everything you do for this football club. Much of your work goes unnoticed, but it is never underestimated. And to the players, thank you for your efforts and the moments we shared. I wish you all the best for the future. I wish nothing but success for Manchester United. This club has been such an important part of my life and that will never change. I will always be proud to have made my contribution and I will always want what is best for him. I’ll be by your side now, watching you from the stands, cheering on the guys.”he wrote.

#1361. Hull City unlikely to keep Vaz beyond January

From a future investment to a potential transfer problem: Robinio Vaz’s time away from Roma risks ending sooner than expected.

The French striker, who moved to Hull City during the final days of the summer transfer window, has failed to establish a significant role in the English side.

According to Tuttomercatoweb.com, the Premier League club is even considering terminating his loan deal early.

Roma acquired Robinio Vaz from Marseille last January for approximately €25 million, banking on the qualities of the 2007-born striker, considered an interesting prospect.

The deal was designed with the player’s future development in mind, but the size of the investment also suggested a potential immediate contribution.

In the second half of the season, however, the Frenchman failed to convince Gian Piero Gasperini, finding very few opportunities to shine. After spending the summer in Rome, the club therefore chose to send him out on loan to help him develop through increased use.

The agreement with Hull City included a €2 million loan with a €30 million option to buy, a deal that could have guaranteed Roma a significant financial return in the event of positive performances. However, things aren’t going as expected.

Vaz continues to find little playing time, and the English club isn’t reportedly considering a permanent purchase of the player.

Instead, the possibility of terminating the deal during the next transfer window has emerged, potentially returning the striker to the Giallorossi early.

Roma is also reportedly dissatisfied with the situation, especially since the lack of playing time risks further slowing the young Frenchman’s development and compromising his value.

The initial goal of the loan was to allow Vaz to gain experience and demonstrate his qualities more consistently, but so far the move to England hasn’t yielded the desired results.

#1359. The best England kits of all time ranked & where to get them cheap on Black Friday

We’ve all got a World Cup 1990 England home shirt kicking around in a draw at home right? There’s a decent chance you’ve also got the red away shirt from the same period, popularised more recently by Jay from The Inbetweeners.

But what if your Three Lions fandom goes a little deeper? The 1982 World Cup squad of Kevin Keegan, Glenn Hoddle and Bryan Robson?

Perhaps you get your kicks from the disappointment of the 93-94 era? Well, the good news is Sports Direct’s range of Score Draw retro England shirts is in rude health, and discounted, in time for Black Friday – although for Football365 England Ladder fans there’s no Phil Neville 2007 shirt – yet (context: his final international appearance).

For the purposes of nostalgia then, here’s an 80s-born England fans top five from a range of 31.

Until the glory of World Cup 2018, I’d only ever seen England win one penalty shootout and it was thanks to the moustachioed ‘safe hands’ David Seaman.

Most people will go to Stuart Pearce’s redemption when they think of that shootout on the way to the Euro 96 semi-finals, but it was Arsenal star Seaman who saved Miguel Angel Nadal’s spot kick, and he did so in a memorable yellow patterned jersey.

Currently reduced by £10 to £51.99, it’s perfect for recreating a famous moment in the garden.

I’m too young to remember the Spain ’82 World Cup, but I watched endless England history and goals videos as a kid and the site of Robson scoring one of the fastest ever World Cup goals in footage that had the contrast turned up just a little too high is etched in my mind.

Perhaps setting me up for decades of disappointment, England romped Group 4 beating France, Czechoslovakia and Kuwait, sending the Three Lions into a second group stage where draws against Spain and West Germany weren’t enough.

England Spain 82 World Cup home and away shirts are on sale here.

Have England ever looked smarter than between 2004 and 2006? The answer is obviously no. And on the pitch, we’d been teased by Michael Owen but now we had Wayne Rooney, Steven Gerrard and David Beckham in his absolute pomp.

The smart collar, the tasteful red stripe across the shoulders. You could (and should) have worn this with a jacket and smart trousers. To a job interview. On your wedding day.

And the football. A spectacularly ill-tempered but crucial 0-0 draw in Turkey ahead of Euro 2004, not to mention Zinedine Zidane’s late show in the opening group game in Portugal and that infamous quarter-final defeat to the hosts.

Before the smart shirt. Before Jordan Pickford in a 2018 penalty shootout, before Jude Bellingham against Slovakia, there was 2002 World Cup David Beckham.

The shirt, a fairly bland white shirt brought to life by an unorthodox vertical thin red stripe up the left-hand side with the England badge overlaying it.

Think Germany 1 England 5, Beckham against Greece, Japan & South Korea, England 1 Argentina 0 and eventually, sadly, a back-pedalling David Seaman as Ronaldinho grinned away.

What a time to be alive, and a bargain with £15 off here.

This is a safe space? Possibly only a psychologist can unravel this, but the 93-94 home shirt was an absolute masterpiece for me. Possibly because I never owned it, and possibly because it was the first time I was properly engrossed in football, but despite not qualifying for World Cup 94 and stinking out Euro 92 either side of letting San Marino score a goal and ****** Ronald Koeman, I ached for this shirt and its extra little badge on the collar.

Why did it have an extra badge on the collar? It actually looks quite odd now.

Still, if you, like me yearn for a time when Wales were closer to qualifying for a tournament than England, this is the one for you.

Quite literally. In 92-93 England were still largely decked out in a version of the World Cup 1990 classics, but there was one right turn of a design choice in 1992 when a sky blue shirt with three huge lions running diagonally down from the left shoulder to the right arm pit was made available.

It was, criminally, only used twice in games against Czechoslovakia and Spain in March and September 1992, although the game against the Spanish in Santander marked Paul Ince’s international debut and Paul Merson’s first international goal came against the Czechs.

#1358. An XI of Man Utd fans who are better than the current Man Utd team

Manchester United‘s worldwide appeal, especially in the early 2000s, means there are plenty of current footballers who were fans of the club in their childhood.

Teams that are 19th in the Premier League don’t tend to have massive fanbases, but welcome to the contradiction that is modern Manchester United.

Here’s an XI of players who supported the club in their youth that are better than the current XI turning out for the club.

Considering some of the keepers United have had in recent years, how they could have used Courtois.

The Belgian keeper, who has become one of the very best, grew up a United fan due to Edwin van der Sar.

“I loved Edwin van der Sar and Casillas,” he told Rio Ferdinand. “So Casillas was because of his young age when he came into the goal at Madrid.

“At my age, I think I was like 12 or 11 at that time. Like I was just starting being goalkeeper. I really also blew my mind. Like, wow, he’s in Real Madrid.

“And I always followed those games. And then I followed always Manchester United for Edwin.”

He even revealed that he was close to joining United before they signed David de Gea.

Now at Lille, Thomas Meunier has long been pinning his colours to the United mast.

In 2017, he said: “I’m a big fan of Manchester United, which remains, in my eyes, the real reference in the world of football.”

And even recently, he said he would cycle to Manchester if given the opportunity.

“If they ever ask me, I’ll cycle there. But maybe it’s better this way. Suppose I play there and have a bad time. I wouldn’t want to hate Manchester United, because I love that club so much.

Akanji said he is “no longer” a United fan after he joined City but sorry Manuel, the internet has receipts.

He told German newspaper NZZ that he had been a United fan “since my childhood days.”

He quickly stopped talking about that since he signed for their city rivals, though.

Dier never outright said he was a United fan, but there are certainly signs.

Mainly, it was who he listed as his idols during an interview with the Players’ Tribune.

“I was a big fan of Roy Keane when I was younger, and then it was Nemanja Vidic (one of the reasons I like the number 15 is Vidic) and his defensive partner, Rio Ferdinand.”

He played a crucial part in City’s most successful ever period* but he was actually a United fan.

Stones has never outright said he grew up a United fan, maybe because the idea of Yorkshiremen doing so is a big no-no, but there is plenty of speculation online that he did indeed support the club.

Before he headed to Brighton, Caicedo named the two clubs in world football he would love to play for.

“In the short term: perform well and get Beerschot out of this plight. And in the long term? I am a fan of Manchester United and Real Madrid. It would be great to play there someday,” he told Gazet van Antwerpen.

A £100 million move to Chelsea has killed that dream for now but it would not be completely out of the question for him one day to be at Old Trafford.

Maddison’s support for United was spearheaded by David Beckham, who was playing for the Old Trafford side when Maddison was at the peak age when kids get drawn into football.

“In my early football days, I was a Manchester United fan and [Beckham] was at the forefront of that,” Maddison told talkSPORT.

“He was the guy on the back of my shirt, I went into the garden practising his free-kicks. The amount of times in school lessons I’d be watching David Beckham free-kicks on YouTube, it was silly really.”

How United could do with Beckham or Maddison now.

Palmer is just about the most famous Manchester United fan playing right now.

There is a picture often circulated online of Palmer as a boy wearing the 2010-11 home kit and in 2024, he confirmed he was a fan of the club as a child.

That fandom has him linked to United every transfer window.

Gibbs-White is another player to tell Rio Ferdinand that he was a United fan.

Speaking on the former United centre-back’s podcast, Gibbs-White picked out Rooney and Scholes as the players he most enjoyed watching.

“Growing up as a kid, I supported Man Utd. [Wayne] Rooney was always my favourite player. He was the key player in that squad. Another player I loved watching was Paul Scholes, he used to just pick the ball up and zing it everywhere.”

This one is a bit of rumour, but Nicky Butt claims that current Liverpool star Ngumoha was actually a United fan.

“I think he was at 13 or 14 or whatever age it was, he goes and looks around Man Utd – whether it be Old Trafford or Carrington,” Butt said on his podcast.

“He’s gone with his family to look around the football club, and then he’s gone to Liverpool. And he’s picked Liverpool, and he’s a Man Utd fan.

“He should not be allowed out of that building before he signed that contract. It would never have happened.”

Since signing for Liverpool, Ngumoha has clearly been told to never mention the United fandom thing.

Scoring in six consecutive matches has clearly made Evanilson confident he could fit in at a Big Six club and he has alerted United to the fact he is a big fan.

Evanilson told Globo Esporte: “So I joke around with Rayan. I think that, here in England, of the big clubs, United are the team I like the most. Rayan said the same thing. When I was a kid, I also used to watch United.

“When Cristiano Ronaldo played for United, I watched loads of his highlights. And, man, knowing that I’m here playing against them…

“It’s a dream, and I tell everyone this in interviews: it was a dream to play at that stadium, and scoring goals is even more important.

“So it’s a dream I’ve been fulfilling, scoring a goal against United because of how big the club is.”

#1355. The 8 highest-paid football pundits in 2026: Sky trio top the list

Punditry work is the lucrative alternative to management for retired ex-footballers and some earn more than a pretty penny for their time.

TV companies want ex-pros to front their coverage and for some audiences, watching the after-match debate has become as entertaining as watching the actual football.

As was the case when they were playing, the best ones get paid the big bucks but who are the biggest earners in football?

We’ve done our best to put together an accurate list but it is worth noting a couple of things. First off, the BBC’s Royal Charter means that they have to declare anyone who receives over £178k so anyone earning below that will not feature in this list.

Another important point to note is that the salaries of TNT pundits like Peter Crouch and Joe Cole are far more secretive than those at Sky.

But with those caveats in mind, here are the top earners in the UK.

Scott is the closest thing we have to Gary Lineker now that the former Match of the Day host has left in that player-turned-pundit-turned-presenter mould.

She has worked with the BBC since 2017, covering her first tournament at the 2018 World Cup, but was not picked as one of the hosts of Match of the Day.

Instead, she has branched out away from sport and also presents The One Show.

Some reports have Redknapp’s salary as high as £750k a year but that seems a little unrealistic.

Redknapp is on the B-tier of Sky Sports pundits, you will rarely see him on the Sunday 4:30pm game but he might be there for a Saturday 5:30.

He has been at Sky for a long time now having joined in 2006, he was even there in the Keys and Gray era, and is also a team captain on A League of Their Own.

Richards has fingers in many pies and so it is hard to nail down exactly what he earns.

What we do know is that he took home £205k from the BBC in their 2022 accounts but he was missing from the 2025/26 report so it must have dipped below £178k.

If we presume that it is still similar, Richards also appears on Sky and CBS, further inflating his pay packet.

To top it off, Richards is also one of the main faces on Gary Lineker’s Stick to Football podcast.

Alan Shearer took a 50k pay cut from 2025 to 2026 but still remains one of the best-paid pundits. With the departure of Gary Lineker, he became the highest-earning sports-related pundit in the BBC but has since lost that accolade.

He’s Match of the Day’s main pundit and was co-commentator for the BBC’s coverage of the World Cup Final this summer.

Rooney became a regular Match of the Day pundit in August 2025 after numerous attempts to stay in the managerial game failed.

Signing for the BBC, he reportedly put pen to paper on a two-year £800k deal.

He was one of the key pundits for the BBC’s World Cup coverage, most memorably calling the extended half-time break “crap”, and has defied doubters to actually be a decent pundit.

He’s currently on a hiatus from his BBC deal as he is being paid a reported £800k to appear on I’m a Celeb.

Would Wayne Rooney have worked in Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona?

“It’s your job,” he famously once said, and his job pays very well.

Keane’s exact contract details are not known but he is rumoured to be earning anywhere from £500k to £1m.

That comes from both his Sky work but also his regular appearances for ITV.

The main man for Monday Night Football ranks second in the best-paid pundits.

Carragher reportedly takes home £1m a year from his Sky deal which sees him feature on every big game as well as plenty of others.

Unlike his partner in crime Neville, Carragher does branch out away from Sky though and is part of CBS Sports’ coverage of the Champions League for US audiences.

Neville is the face of Sky Sports’ football coverage.

He reinvented the punditry role following his retirement in 2011 and if his early Monday Night Football performances were a little too high-pitched and awkward, he soon transformed into the perfect pundit.

These days, he has jumped the shark somewhat and is becoming increasingly depressed at Manchester United but his Stick to Football podcast has been backed by Global and Disney+.

For his Sky contract alone he is reported to be taking home £1.1m a year, making him the best-paid pundit in the UK.

#1354. The top 10 goalscorers worldwide in 2026: Harry Kane 3rd but outscored by forgotten England man

Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Al-Ahli and Dinamo Zagreb are among the clubs represented in the worldwide top 10 goalscorers of 2026.

There are some familiar superstar names alongside prolific forwards from leagues you might struggle to find on a map, with a few rather unexpected players outscoring some of Europe’s biggest stars. Lionel Messi has scored 30 goals for Inter Miami in 2026, but he just misses out on the top 10.

Here are the 10 most prolific club goalscorers in world football this calendar year, across all competitions.

A player you’ve (probably) never heard of. Get used to that.

Gambian midfielder Ousman Gai averages a goal every 60 minutes in 2026, which is the best ratio of any player in this top 10.

He finished as the top scorer in the Philippines Football League last season, firing Manila Digger to the league title, a return that earned him a move to Cambodian outfit Visakha in the summer.

We all love a journeyman Brazilian playing in a far-flung league, don’t we?

Chigor is a classic of the genre, having developed his skills in the Red Bull system and gone on to play for the energy brand’s Bragantino club.

After representing eight clubs in Brazil, the forward moved to Thailand in 2024 and is currently leading the line for Malaysian outfit Selangor. He’s scored 34 goals in just 33 appearances for the club in 2026.

The most prolific goalscorer you’ve never heard of.

After some short-lived loans in South Korea and Portugal as a youngster, Bergson spent most of his twenties moving around Brazil without making much of an impression.

But he found a settled home at Malaysian giants Johor Darul Ta’zim since signing for the club as a 30-year-old back in 2021. He’s notched an insane tally of 203 goals in 200 appearances for the club and shows little sign of slowing down, with 34 in 2026 so far.

The former Brazil youth international was recently cleared by FIFA to switch his allegiance to represent Malaysia, and he’s already scored a hat-trick for the national team against Singapore.

Not that one. The former Barcelona and Liverpool man has scored a few for Inter Miami this year, but he’s slowing down considerably in his twilight years.

No, this is the Colombian one, once of Watford, who is now taking Viktor Gyokeres’ place in scoring for fun at Manchester United.

He’d be even higher if he’d converted both of the penalties he took against Manchester United in midweek.

You remember him. The World Cup cult hero and surprise 2026 Ballon d’Or nominee won the Saudi Pro League Golden Boot last season, having notched five more goals than Al-Nassr title-winner Cristiano Ronaldo.

Quinoses has scored 36 goals for Al-Qadsiah this calendar year, although he’s not quite the top Saudi-based goalscorer of 2026. It’s not Ronaldo – can you guess who?

Keep this up and you wonder if a European club might take a punt on the 29-year-old Mexico international.

The 23-year-old Puerto Rican has recently moved to DS Edusoccer after an outrageous goalscoring return for Academia Quintana.

Seven(!) goals in one game help out quite a bit here. He scored them in an 18-1(!!) victory over FC Mayaguez.

The oldest player in this top 10, Zampedri earned his first two senior Chile caps last year after blossoming in his mid-thirties with Universidad Catolica.

He was born and raised in Argentina but switched international allegiance after thriving in the country’s top flight over the past few years.

The 38-year-old has fired Universidad Catolica to two Primera Division de Chile league titles and won the Golden Boot in each of the last six seasons, with a seventh pretty much in the bag for 2026.

You knew he’d be here. Comfortably the top goalscorer when it comes to major European football in 2026. And he’s even further ahead if you count his bounty of goals for England.

Kane isn’t the England international with the most club goals in 2026, somehow.

Toney was pipped to the Saudi Pro League by Quinoses last season, but he’s the early frontrunner this season with 14 goals from just 10 appearances this season.

That takes his overall tally to 44 goals this calendar year for Al Ahli. Every chance he tops this list when all is said and done come New Year’s Day.

It’ll be interesting to see whether he has another Premier League stint in him. Given his goalscoring output, you’d take a punt, wouldn’t you? Whether he’d be willing to take a wage cut is another question – but maybe when his current deal expires in 2028.

We expected the leader to be a total unknown playing in the middle of nowhere, but Beljo is actually somewhat established.

The 24-year-old is a full Croatia international with experience playing in a top European league, although he failed to pull up any trees in the Bundesliga with Augsburg.

He’s been outrageously prolific since returning to Croatia with the perennial champions Dinamo Zagreb in 2025. He notched 38 goals in all competitions in his debut season and appears set to better that tally in year two.

Beljo recently scored against Sunderland in the Europa League. Keep this up, and another opportunity at a higher level will surely come calling. Leeds United are among a host of clubs who have been linked.

#1353. Sportword: Play daily football word game on Planet Sport

Sportword is Planet Sport’s game which challenges you to guess football and other sport-related words within six attempts.

As you might have guessed, it’s the football version we’re hosting here on Planet Football, adding to our hundreds of other football quizzes many of you already play daily, including our type-in-the-answer list quizzes and our complete-the-football-line-up quizzes.

We are busy building a new home for Sportword and all our other sport games and quizzes, but in the meantime, you can play the daily football game right here so please bookmark this page, try today’s word and then come back tomorrow.

Simply put, you have six attempts to guess a word. There will be a clue for each one to focus your mind a little.

Type in your first guess then hit enter. Each tile will change colour to indicate if the letter is in the correct position, elsewhere in the word or does not appear at all. A green tile means the letter is in the correct position; an orange tile means the letter is elsewhere in the word; a grey tile means that letter is not in the word at all.

If you are struggling, you will see a hint button that becomes available from your fourth attempt. Clicking it will reveal a tile, though note this is only available to logged-in users.

You can also click Give Up if you’re really struggling and just want to be put out of your misery. It’s not one for the purists, but it’s nice to have the option!

As with all our other football quizzes, we also have a leaderboard that ranks players by the number of attempts and time they required to guess the correct word.

We will be launching rugby, rugby league and tennis versions in the future too, and in our soon-to-launch games hub you’ll be able to play sub-categories, for example 2000s Premier League players. #1352. Alejandro Garnacho's nightmare Aston Villa loan continues: Struggling star is left at home as Unai Emery picks TWO goalkeepers on bench for Galatasaray defeat before sending warning to ex-Man United winger

Published: 17:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 17:05 EST, 24 November 2026

Alejandro Garnacho's future at Aston Villa was plunged into further doubt on Tuesday as he was overlooked for their defeat at Galatasaray.

The Argentine joined on loan from Chelsea last summer with a £43million obligation to buy, triggered when certain targets were hit.

Yet Garnacho has yet to start for Villa and was not even on the bench in Istanbul, even though two goalkeepers were named.

Asked whether Garnacho was fit for this match, Villa boss Unai Emery said: 'Today I think the best players to play with us, to be with us, were here.'

Daily Mail Sport has reported regularly this season that Garnacho may not see out his loan spell and now that looks increasingly likely to be the case.

There is not thought to be a break clause in the loan but if Chelsea and Villa agreed to cancel it, that would allow Garnacho to go elsewhere in January.

Alejandro Garnacho was not in the Aston Villa squad for their defeat at Galatasaray on Tuesday

Villa boss Unai Emery chose to include two goalkeepers on his bench instead of picking of him

Villa had a similar situation with Harvey Elliott. The midfielder joined on loan from Liverpool in summer 2025 but barely played.

Emery decided quickly that he did not want to sign Elliott permanently and could not risk triggering the appearance clause that would have seen him join Villa for £35m.

Villa are now without a win in six and Emery admitted: 'The next challenge against PSG at home will be huge. If we can recover the three points we lost today maybe we still have a chance to reach the top eight but we are not favourites.'

Emery also bemoaned the home side's time-wasting tactics after Deniz Gul headed them into a 77th-minute lead.

He said: 'I am not blaming the referee but he was unfair with us by adding only five minutes. After they scored it was impossible to play.'

#1351. Sublime England thrash Croatia in best performance for a decade

If this is Tuchel-ball, if this is the way Thomas Tuchel wants England to play, then yes, please. More of the same; bring it on. The standard is set.

England’s DNA? This was a total-football annihilation of a top nation. Croatia, 14th in the world and fierce competitors, were cowed and humiliated at home in this Nations League tie. This was the biggest defeat in their proud history – seventh heaven for England, and hell for the hosts.

The visitors were sublime. Harry Kane (twice – 89 goals now for his country), Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon all scored and were outstanding. Bukayo Saka also struck twice. Alex Scott made his first start and will take some dislodging. The Bournemouth midfielder was slick with a snap – perpetual, intelligent, smooth motion.

Harry Kane at the DOUBLE! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿The Three Lions have FIVE in Rijeka 🦁 pic.twitter.com/BRnVXADtHC

Luka Modric has had the most extraordinary career but he was emphatically second best here and was subbed off on 57 minutes at 5-0. He looked bereft, having had Scott and Elliot Anderson run all over him and Mateo Kovacic.

We came out of the World Cup wondering if Tuchel really had an idea of how he can get England over the line. After last Saturday’s defeat by world and European champions Spain, followed by Tuesday’s win over the Czech Republic we still did not know.

But here the standard was set – it was an exhilarating example of the football England are capable of. On display we saw the speed, the movement, the passes under pressure, the ambition, the control and aggression. This was the full package. Bottle it. Bag it. Believe it.

Croatia have an ageing team and are in transition, but they were left looking callow. It looked as though it was men against boys. There were plenty of boys in the stands, with 6,200 children allowed in for what was supposed to be a behind-closed-doors fixture – Croatia’s punishment for crowd trouble.

Their new head coach Slaven Bilic would doubtless have been relieved that the match was not played in front of the usual, passionate, partisan crowd. Even then some of the kids booed and left early. Bilic looked shell-shocked. As well he might.

And Saka makes it FOUR! ⚽️⚽️⚽️⚽️England break to devastating effect - Croatia are reeling... pic.twitter.com/60EgNt4cfh

It was 4-0 at half-time. It could easily have been 7-1 – Kovacic missed a sitter for Croatia at 3-0 and Gordon should have had a hat-trick. How significant is it that England’s three most dangerous players do not play in the Premier League? Probably not very. But the fact they turn out for Real Madrid, Barcelona and Bayern Munich is. They performed like the top players their clubs think they clearly are.

Gordon heads in to make it THREE! 💥England are cruising 🛳️ pic.twitter.com/nqwUxFmkof

Kane’s commitment was incredible. At one stage Croatia substitute Kristijan Jakić threatened to break clear but was stopped by England’s last man tracking back. It was Kane, one cap short of equalling Peter Shilton’s all-time record of 125 appearances, and it was already 5-0 when that happened.

These could be exciting times for England. Times when they have shaken off the debate over how well or otherwise they did at the World Cup and moved on. Tuchel has talked up that third-place finish; we have tended to dwell on the semi-final exit to Argentina.

And now? If Tuchel does go and win a trophy for England, he will be talking about this game. Previously he referenced the 5-0 demolition of Serbia in Belgrade, during the World Cup qualification. But the Serbians were a rabble. Croatia are not, but were made to look so on Saturday.

Where will this sit among England performances? There was the 2-1 victory away to Italy at the beginning of the Euro 2024 qualification campaign in March 2023. Before that, the 3-2 win away to Spain in 2018, also in the Nations League. But England were more thrilling here. Do we have to go back to 5-1 in Munich in 2001?

The concern will be the familiar England problem of looking like world-beaters in the autumn and worn out by the time a tournament comes around in the summer. But against Croatia there was control and authority as they raised their chances of finishing in the top two and qualifying for next March’s quarter-finals.

The goals rained in – even if the best remained the first as Marc Guéhi intercepted a clearance, Scott took the ball on the half-turn and found Bellingham. He slid it through to Kane who finished high into the net. What a goal.

Bellingham ➡️ Kane! ⚽️The Three Lions lead in Rijeka with their first shot on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/ZLcnGLvj3z

England were swarming all over Croatia. Saka crossed, Gordon took the ball down and turned it back for Bellingham to stab home.

What a touch from Anthony Gordon! 🔥The Barca man squares it to the Real Madrid man and England lead 2-0 ⚽️⚽️ pic.twitter.com/31Y1Ojx44M

Gordon, after twice being denied, got his goal – with another header, as against the Czechs. This time Jarell Quansah, back in ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold, delivered from the right and Gordon met it to score for the fourth successive game for England. Even before half-time England were not finished as Bellingham crossed low from the left and found Saka, who found the back of the net.

After the break, the hunger remained insatiable. Anderson was sent down the right and Kane slid in. Croatia then lost the ball sloppily inside their own area, Kane thought about shooting but unselfishly fed Saka, who claimed a second goal.

Saka should have had a hat-trick before substitute Morgan Rogers wrapped up the scoring, collecting a ball over the top from the relentless Bellingham – once again captain after Kane went off – and finishing with ease after rounding the goalkeeper. It was a third assist for Bellingham and a seventh goal for England. It could have been double figures.

SEVENTH heaven for England! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿Morgan Rogers is the latest player to put his name on the scoresheet... ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/H5txZRVgLC

Absolutely [that was the 90-minute performance we’ve been looking for]. Maybe three minutes after the three-zero there was a big mistake [Kovacic’s chance] and some easy ball losses but that was a performance of the highest level from everyone. And from the first until the last minute from everyone who started and everyone who came on. Congratulations to the team.

Very, very impressive [to do this] on an away pitch. We created so many chances in the first 40 minutes. We were so fluid from the start. I looked at the clock and thought ‘Oh, this has been a good three minutes, this has been a good seven minutes…’ and it never stopped.

We kept the pace up and played through the gaps, stayed hungry in our counter-pressing and defending.

We played humble and always got the basics right.

Unbelievable from start to finish. We spoke a lot about having a 90-minute game in which we were dominant with and without the ball and that was it out there. We’re at our best when we’re brave and we’re physically overpowering. When we make it a Premier League game and they couldn’t live with our pace, our movement, our runs. And we were clinical.

There’s freedom. All four of us [him, Bellingham, Saka and Gordon] can play in the 10 pocket, play as the nine. I can play as a midfielder. We’re good enough and smart enough so if we lose the ball we can cover in midfield and defence. That’s the way we want to play. It’s so hard for them to pick a man and press. Every man was at the highest level.

Beautiful hotel, lovely weather, we could easily have fallen into that holiday mode. It’s an unusual situation for us. We’ve never been away this long in this kind of camp and that’s the perfect end to the week,

[And now to equal Peter Shilton’s record 125th cap on Tuesday?] That would be nice. That’s why he keeps taking me off, to rest me for the next game. That’s what he said to me after. I’ll be ready to start on Tuesday.

An amazing night for us. We came out from the start on top and played with high energy and we punished them.

It was special and fun to play. We were really clinical today. Two goals for England is always a nice feeling.

We showed the hunger, passion and quality we had. A mixture of everything we wanted to show.

[Bellingham] was amazing tonight. He deserved man of the match and deserves to be player of the year.

At least the Croatia fans did not seem too dispirited, the kids smiling and waving at the camera, despite the utter trouncing their team took.

England were terrific but how much of that was because Croatia were terrible will be open to debate.
